groups.title: pr-first-merge: auto-merge reporting doesn't read the actual check conclusion
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

The pr-first integration path's auto-merge convention (`_shared/pr-first-merge.md`, or the calling skill that invokes it) calls `gh pr merge {n} --auto --squash` when a PR's status checks are still `IN_PROGRESS`, then reports the outcome as "merged once CI passed" based solely on the PR's `state` transitioning to `MERGED`. `gh pr merge --auto` merges immediately once GitHub's own merge-readiness conditions are satisfied — which, on a repository with no *required* status checks configured, can mean immediately, regardless of whether an in-progress check later passes or fails. The reporting language ("queue an auto-merge so it merges once that passes") implies the merge is gated on that specific check's conclusion, but nothing in the sequence ever reads that check's final `conclusion` field to confirm it actually passed before or as part of the merge. Concretely observed: `test` check `IN_PROGRESS` at 18:50:21Z, "I'll queue an auto-merge so it merges once that passes" at 18:50:28Z, `gh pr merge --auto --squash` at 18:50:31Z, PR `state: MERGED` at `mergedAt: 2026-09-20T18:50:30Z` — merged 9 seconds after the check was last observed in progress, with no subsequent read of that check's conclusion.

## Deliverables

- In `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` (or wherever the `--auto` merge call and its result reporting are documented), require reading the relevant status check's `conclusion` (via `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`) after a `gh pr merge --auto` call resolves to `MERGED`, and state explicitly in the reported outcome whether the check had actually completed and passed by then, or whether the repository has no required checks and the merge proceeded independent of the check's state.
- Note in that file that `gh pr merge --auto` on a repo with no required checks is not equivalent to "wait for checks to pass" — name this distinction explicitly so a caller doesn't infer gating behavior that isn't there.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A caller following `_shared/pr-first-merge.md`'s auto-merge procedure reads and reports the actual check conclusion (or its absence/irrelevance) rather than inferring "merged once CI passed" from the PR's `state` field alone.
- The file states plainly whether this repository's branch protection requires the `test` check before merge, so future callers don't have to re-derive that fact per-run.

## Technical Approach

Locate the `--auto`-merge call site in `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` and add a post-merge (or, where the merge is not yet resolved, a post-arm) read of `gh pr view {n} --json statusCheckRollup` to extract the named check's `conclusion`. Compose the reported outcome from that read rather than from the PR's `state` alone: "merged, {check} concluded {conclusion}" when a required check resolved before merge, or "merged — this repository has no required status checks, so the merge did not wait on {check}'s outcome" when it doesn't. Add a one-time note near the top of the auto-merge procedure documenting this repository's actual branch-protection configuration (required checks or their absence) so this doesn't need re-deriving per run.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge.md` — the `--auto` merge call and its result-reporting language

## Gotchas

- This is a reporting-fidelity fix, not a merge-mechanics change — do not add an actual wait-for-check-conclusion gate unless the record's own scope is later widened; the Acceptance Criteria only ask for accurate reporting of what already happened.
- Verify the actual branch-protection state (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection` or the repo settings UI) rather than assuming from this record's evidence alone — the observed 9-second merge is consistent with "no required checks" but should be confirmed directly before documenting it as fact.

groups.title: Multi-spec review verdict PR comment: later spec silently overwrites earlier spec's verdict
groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Current State

`plugin/skills/_shared/pr-run-comments.md`'s `verdict` comment kind uses one marker
(`<!-- run-comment: verdict -->`) per PR, found-and-updated-in-place per its "Post-or-update
procedure" — designed for a single-spec run where a re-triggered review edits the same comment.

A multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow` run shares one PR across every spec (`flow/multi-spec.md`).
Each spec's own `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 7 posts this same `verdict`-marked comment
independently. Observed directly on run `2026-09-18T054643-spec-2580-2581` (PR #2586, records
#2580 and #2581): #2580's review posted a verdict comment; #2581's review, following the exact
same documented procedure, found the existing marker and updated it in place — silently
replacing #2580's verdict content with #2581's. Nothing in `pr-run-comments.md` names this
multi-spec case or says what should happen instead.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide the intended multi-spec shape for the `verdict` comment kind: one comment per spec
      (would need a spec-qualified marker, e.g. `<!-- run-comment: verdict:{spec} -->`, and a
      change to the "one comment per kind per run" framing), or one running combined comment
      that each spec's review appends its own section to rather than replacing the whole body.
- [ ] Update `pr-run-comments.md`'s Comment kinds / Post-or-update procedure to document the
      chosen shape explicitly for multi-spec runs, the same way `flow/multispec-pr-checklist.md`
      already documents the phase-checklist's own multi-spec (cumulative, never-reset) shape.
- [ ] Update `review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 7's verdict-comment composition instructions to
      match.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A second spec's review verdict in a multi-spec run no longer silently discards the first
   spec's verdict content from the PR's `verdict` comment.
2. `pr-run-comments.md` states the multi-spec behavior explicitly, mirroring how it already
   states the single-spec re-run-edits-in-place behavior.

## Release Note

Fixed the multi-spec Review verdict PR comment silently overwriting an earlier spec's verdict in the same run.

## Technical Approach

Recommend the spec-qualified-marker shape (`<!-- run-comment: verdict:{spec} -->`, one comment
per spec) over the appended-sections alternative: `pr-run-comments.md`'s existing Post-or-update
procedure already finds-and-updates by exact marker text, so a spec-qualified marker reuses that
same find-or-create logic unchanged per spec, whereas the appended-sections shape needs new
logic to locate and replace only this spec's own section within a shared comment body without
disturbing siblings' sections — more moving parts for the same outcome. This is a
recommendation for the build to weigh, not a foreclosed decision — the Deliverables above still
name both candidates.

Whichever shape is chosen, `review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 7's comment-composition call
(`<!-- run-comment: verdict -->` as currently hardcoded) needs the spec identifier threaded
into the marker it composes, and `pr-run-comments.md`'s Comment kinds table (currently listing
`verdict` as a single per-PR marker) needs its multi-spec behavior stated explicitly, the same
way `flow/multispec-pr-checklist.md` already documents the phase-checklist's cumulative shape
for the same multi-spec-shared-PR situation.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-run-comments.md` — Comment kinds table (`verdict` row) and the
  Post-or-update procedure
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 7's verdict-comment composition (the
  `<!-- run-comment: verdict -->` literal)

## Gotchas

- The chosen shape must not break `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s or any other consumer's expectation
  that the `verdict` marker is a single, PR-wide comment kind — grep for `run-comment: verdict`
  across `plugin/skills/**/*.md` before finalizing the shape, to catch any other reader of this
  marker beyond the two files named above.
- This is a real, live-observed bug (not a hypothetical) — a regression test reproducing the
  two-spec-same-PR sequence (post spec A's verdict, then post spec B's verdict, assert both
  survive in some form) is worth adding alongside the fix, not just a unit test on the
  marker-matching logic in isolation.

groups.title: shaping-mode.md, capture/SKILL.md, and refine-mode.md's shaped-body prose still name only three required sections
groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Current State

`plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md`'s Read-back verification step,
`plugin/skills/capture/SKILL.md`'s Shaped-body branch, and
`plugin/skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s spec-shaped-body check (used to
build a live flag-back comment) all restate `_shared/work-record.md`'s
spec-shaped-body check in prose (per `plugin/bin/lib/compose-record/compose.js`'s
own header comment) as a three-section check (Current State, Deliverables,
Acceptance Criteria). #2580 added a fourth required section, `## Release
Note`, to the mechanical definition (`_shared/work-record.md`,
`compose-record/compose.js`'s `REQUIRED_SECTIONS`) but did not touch these
three files' own prose restatements, since none is a blocking dependency for
#2580's own Acceptance Criteria (the two mechanical gates —
`materialize-format.js`'s hard gate and `compose-record/compose.js`'s
`validateShaped` — are unaffected by what a human-facing prose checklist
says; `compose-subject.js`'s merge-time gate still catches an under-shaped
record regardless of what any of these three prose checks say).

`refine-mode.md`'s case is the same class of gap but with live behavior: its
check auto-downgrades a `ready` row to flag-back with a message listing
"missing/empty" sections — until fixed, a record missing only `## Release
Note` passes this check silently (no flag-back), and would only be caught
later, at merge time, by `compose-subject.js`'s unconditional gate.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Update `shaping-mode.md`'s Read-back verification prose to name all
      four required sections
- [ ] Update `capture/SKILL.md`'s Shaped-body branch prose to name all four
      required sections
- [ ] Update `refine-mode.md`'s spec-shaped-body check prose (and its
      flag-back comment's missing-section enumeration) to name all four
      required sections

## Acceptance Criteria

1. None of the three files' prose restatements of the spec-shaped-body check
   omits `## Release Note`
2. A `ready` record whose only gap is a missing/empty `## Release Note`
   section is flagged back by `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine`'s check, the
   same way a missing `## Current State` already is

## Release Note

Kept three authoring-time human checklists in sync with the four-section spec-shaped-body definition.

## Technical Approach

Each file restates the same underlying `_shared/work-record.md` definition independently in
prose (none calls a shared function for this human-facing description), so this is three
small, independent one-clause edits — no shared helper to touch, no behavioral change beyond
what each restatement names.

- `shaping-mode.md:69` says spec-shaped-body's structural minimum is "Current State,
  Deliverables, and Acceptance Criteria" and that `_shared/work-record.md`'s check
  "re-verifies exactly these three" — change to name four, including `## Release Note`.
- `capture/SKILL.md:260` detects a "shaped" body as containing `## Current State`,
  `## Deliverables`, and exactly one of `## Acceptance Criteria` / `## Open Question` — add
  `## Release Note` to the required set (`## Open Question` is capture's own alternate-AC
  form and is unaffected by this record's scope otherwise).
- `refine-mode.md:239` describes the check as verifying "`## Current State`, `## Deliverables`,
  and `## Acceptance Criteria` are present and each non-empty" — add `## Release Note` to this
  sentence. The flag-back comment template at line 244/249 already substitutes a dynamic
  `{list}`/`$MISSING_LIST` computed from whichever sections are actually missing — no template
  change needed there, only the prose describing which sections that computation checks.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md` — line 69's three-section restatement
- `plugin/skills/capture/SKILL.md` — line 260's Shaped-body detection prose
- `plugin/skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` — line 239's spec-shaped-body check description

## Gotchas

- These are three independent, out-of-sync prose copies of the same underlying check (no
  shared function) — verify each edit against the *current* line numbers at build time, since
  intervening commits between this record's authoring and its build may have shifted them.

groups.title: Fixture-repo end-to-end regression test for /flow's two-call handoff run-dir bookkeeping (#1826 AC1/AC4/AC5 follow-up)
groups.body:
Surface: infra

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

#1826 (this record's parent) fixed the two specific silent-degrade gaps its own diagnosis confirmed: the Manifesto's `config.yml` write logged no absolute path (#1810's occurrence), and no conditional skip on that write path logged a `SKIP` entry, and `steps-and-gates.md`'s case 3 recomputed levers fresh from the precedence chain instead of preferring `decisions.md`'s own snapshot header, and its prose assumed interruption rather than also covering a completed-but-config-missing first call.

What #1826 explicitly called for but this pass did not build: a genuine end-to-end regression test simulating a `/flow` two-call dispatch handoff (`build,test` then `review,polish,wrap-up` sharing one `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`) against a real fixture repo — bare git remote for the push/PR half, `gh` mocked at the injectable-runner seam — asserting the anchored run directory's actual `config.yml`/`decisions.md`/`run-state.json` contents after call 1, and a companion fixture where the claim step is skipped and a build commit must never happen.

Investigation during #1826 found `tests/dispatch-flow-rundir-handoff.test.js` (the file #1826's own Gotchas assumed already had this fixture machinery) is entirely prose-conformance-based — it regex-matches skill `.md` files, with no bare-repo/mocked-`gh` runtime simulation anywhere in the suite. The underlying units this test would exercise are each already well-covered in isolation (`plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js`'s `computeAdoption` case 3 logic — `tests/bin-lib/flow/preflight.test.js`; `bin/claim-targets.js`'s contest/all-or-abort handling — `tests/bin-lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.test.js`, including the exact "second target live → first released, exit 3" shape AC5 wants), but nothing ties them together end-to-end the way `/flow`'s own Step 1→2.8→3→4 sequence actually runs.

## Deliverables

- Build a fixture-repo harness (bare `origin` remote, a temp worktree-like checkout, `gh` faked at the same injectable-runner seam `tests/bin-lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.test.js` already uses) that runs the real sequence: `bin/materialize.js` → `bin/claim-targets.js` → `bin/set-config.js` (the Manifesto's batch write) → `bin/hooks.js record-worktree` → the PR-early push+draft-PR procedure (mocked `gh pr create`/`gh pr list`).
- Assert the anchored run directory's `config.yml`, `decisions.md`, and `run-state.json` (with `worktree` and `pr` fields) all exist and carry correct content after this simulated "call 1."
- A companion fixture where the claim step (`bin/claim-targets.js`) exits non-zero (contested) — assert the harness never reaches the materialize/commit step for that case.
- A companion fixture reproducing the shadow-write hypothesis: a `config.yml` written under `<worktree>/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run}/` instead of the anchored `$RUN_ROOT` path — assert this is detected (or made structurally impossible by the harness's own path construction).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The new fixture-repo test(s) actually exercise the real `bin/` CLIs listed above (not a re-statement of their own existing unit tests) and pass.
- `npm test` passes.
- The test(s) live alongside `tests/dispatch-flow-rundir-handoff.test.js` or in a clearly-named sibling file.

## Technical Approach

Reuse `tests/bin-lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.test.js`'s injectable-runner fake-`gh` pattern rather than inventing a new one. A real `git init --bare` temp directory as `origin`, plus a real temp working checkout, gives the push/PR half something real to push against without touching the network.

### Key Files

- `tests/dispatch-flow-rundir-handoff.test.js` — natural home, or a named sibling
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js`, `plugin/bin/claim-targets.js`, `plugin/bin/set-config.js`, `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — the real CLIs to orchestrate
- `tests/bin-lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.test.js` — the injectable-runner fake-`gh` pattern to reuse

## Gotchas

- This is genuinely new test infrastructure, not a small addition — size it as its own build, not a quick follow-up task.
- Keep the fixture read-only against the real repo; everything happens in a temp directory.

## Original request

Filed as a scoped follow-up from #1826's own AC1/AC4/AC5 (the end-to-end regression test its Deliverables called for), which #1826 itself did not build — see its own Current State for why (investigation found the fixture machinery its Gotchas assumed already existed does not).

groups.title: build: a record whose deliverables are all already on the base branch still opens a bookkeeping-only PR instead of stopping with a close proposal
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

When `/claude-tweaks:build` (inside a dispatched `/claude-tweaks:flow`) finds every deliverable of a record already present on the base branch, it has no documented "already shipped" exit. Instead it commits a "verified already implemented, no code changes" plan doc, opens a draft PR carrying only bookkeeping files, and the pipeline runs test, review, polish and wrap-up through to `pending-review` instead of stopping and staging a Close proposal for the record.

Observed in this repo, 2026-09-14: record #2028 had already been shipped by PR #2234 (merged 2026-09-12; PR title ends "(#2028, #2032)", commit message says `refs #2028`). The queue pull's shipped-candidate exclusion did not catch it (#2449 tracks that separate miss). The dispatched flow (run `2026-09-14T212627-record-2028`) then:

1. Materialized the spec and found "every deliverable and acceptance criterion in the materialized spec is already present in pack.js/console-resolve.js and already covered by (#2028)-tagged tests."
2. Committed a plan doc saying so, because the build skill has no rule for this case — the run's own grep of `build/*.md` and `flow/*.md` for "already implemented", "no code changes", "nothing to build" found nothing, so the agent improvised a verification-only commit.
3. Opened draft PR #2497 via the pr-early lifecycle: five `chore:` commits, two doc files, zero implementation lines.
4. Ran the full test suite twice, reviewed the "bookkeeping-only" diff as PASS, derived ceremony down to fast-lane, filed two flaky-test issues, and reported `OUTCOME: pending-review`.

Cost: 34 minutes and about $11.50 of headless runtime for a PR that then has to be closed unmerged by a human, on a record that had already been verified as already-shipped twice before (a backlog-refine needs-decision comment and a prior run's wrap-up comment both recommended closing it).

## Deliverables

- Give `/claude-tweaks:build`'s implementation-assessment step a documented "already shipped" exit: when every deliverable and acceptance criterion is satisfied on the base branch with zero implementation diff needed, stop with a distinct outcome (e.g. `OUTCOME: already-shipped`) instead of proceeding to a bookkeeping-only commit.
- On that outcome, stage the same Close proposal the queue-pull shipped-candidate exclusion (#1984/#1892's machinery) already stages for the pre-dispatch case, so the two "already shipped" detection points converge on one proposal shape.
- Avoid opening a PR for this outcome — or, if the pr-early lifecycle has already opened a draft PR by the point the already-shipped exit is detected, close that draft PR rather than leaving it open.
- Release the record's claim on this exit path.
- Ensure the second `review,polish,wrap-up` dispatch call is never made for a run that exits `already-shipped` at the first (`build,test`) call — dispatch's report should surface this as a no-op, not a `pending-review` PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record whose materialized spec's every deliverable and acceptance criterion is already satisfied on the base branch, with zero implementation diff required, exits `build` with `OUTCOME: already-shipped` — no bookkeeping-only commit, no draft PR left open.
- The same run stages a Close proposal for the record (reusing the shipped-candidate exclusion's proposal shape) and releases the record's claim.
- `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s two-call sequencing skips the second (`review,polish,wrap-up`) call entirely when the first call reports `already-shipped`, and its own report surfaces the record as a no-op rather than `pending-review`.
- A reproduction fixture built from the #2028/PR#2234 shape (deliverables/AC already satisfied, zero-diff materialization) exercises the new exit path.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Add an "already shipped" check to build's implementation-assessment step, run after materialization confirms the spec against the base branch: if every Deliverables/Acceptance Criteria item is already satisfied with no code diff needed, short-circuit before any commit or PR-open step, emit `OUTCOME: already-shipped`, and hand off to the same Close-proposal staging path #1984/#2449's shipped-candidate machinery already produces (reuse, don't reimplement, the proposal shape). Wire dispatch's sequential-execution logic to read this outcome from the first call and skip minting the second `review,polish,wrap-up` Task call when it fires — the same kind of outcome-gated branching `dispatch/sequential-execution.md` already uses for other early-exit outcomes. If a draft PR was already opened by the pr-early lifecycle before this check runs, close it as part of the same exit (never leave a bookkeeping-only draft PR open for a human to find and close by hand).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — the implementation-assessment step gaining the `already-shipped` exit
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/sequential-execution.md` — the two-call dispatch orchestration that must skip the second call on this outcome
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js` — the existing Close-proposal shape to reuse, not reimplement
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` — the draft-PR-open step this exit may need to close
- `tests/` — a fixture pinning the #2028/PR#2234 shape (zero-diff materialization → `already-shipped`)

## Gotchas

- This is a distinct gap from #2449 (the pre-dispatch shipped-candidate exclusion missing #1892/PR#2287) — that fix prevents dispatch from ever picking an already-shipped record in the first place; this record's fix is the backstop for when a record still reaches `build` despite that. Both should converge on the same Close-proposal shape, but neither replaces the other.
- Don't judge the fix by "the merge would have been safe anyway" — the cost here (34 minutes, ~$11.50, a PR a human has to close by hand) is the defect, independent of whether the underlying content was harmless.

## Original request

build: a record whose deliverables are all already on the base branch still opens a bookkeeping-only PR instead of stopping with a close proposal

**Summary:** When `/claude-tweaks:build` (inside a dispatched `/claude-tweaks:flow`) finds every deliverable of a record already present on the base branch, it commits a "verified already implemented, no code changes" plan doc, opens a draft PR carrying only bookkeeping files, and the pipeline runs test, review, polish and wrap-up to `pending-review` instead of stopping and staging a Close proposal for the record.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `/claude-tweaks:build` (inside `/claude-tweaks:flow`'s two-call `build,test` then `review,polish,wrap-up` dispatch)

**Use case:**

Observed in thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks itself (public), 2026-09-14. Record #2028 had already been shipped by PR #2234 (merged 2026-09-12; PR title ends "(#2028, #2032)", commit message says `refs #2028`). The queue pull's shipped-candidate exclusion did not catch it (#2449 tracks that miss). The dispatched flow, run `2026-09-14T212627-record-2028`, then:

1. Materialized the spec and found "every deliverable and acceptance criterion in the materialized spec is already present in pack.js/console-resolve.js and already covered by (#2028)-tagged tests".
2. Committed a plan doc saying so, because the build skill has no rule for this case. The run's own grep of `build/*.md` and `flow/*.md` for "already implemented", "no code changes", "nothing to build" found nothing, so the agent improvised a verification-only commit.
3. Opened draft PR #2497 via the pr-early lifecycle: five `chore:` commits, two doc files, zero implementation lines.
4. Ran the full test suite twice, reviewed a "bookkeeping-only" diff as PASS, derived ceremony down to fast-lane, filed two flaky-test issues, and reported `OUTCOME: pending-review`.

Cost: 34 minutes and about $11.50 of headless runtime for a PR that then has to be closed unmerged by a human, on a record that had already been verified as already-shipped twice before (a backlog-refine needs-decision comment and a prior run's wrap-up comment both recommended closing it).

What the plugin should do instead: build's implementation assessment needs a documented "already shipped" exit. When every deliverable and acceptance criterion is satisfied on the base branch with zero implementation diff needed, the flow should stop with a distinct outcome (for example `OUTCOME: already-shipped`), stage the same Close proposal the queue-pull exclusion stages, avoid opening a PR (or close the draft PR the pr-early lifecycle already opened), release the record's claim, and let dispatch's report surface it as a no-op rather than a pending-review PR. The second `review,polish,wrap-up` call should never be dispatched for such a run.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.125.0

groups.title: dispatch/settle-and-merge.md: missing-claim fallback to pending-review is overridable by a subagent's own risk judgment
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s second-call template instructs the dispatched review call to check the record's live claim state before choosing among `merged`/`armed`/`pending-review`/`ready-to-merge`, with explicit language: *"If the claim's `runId` no longer matches this run, or is not `live`, or `bot:in-progress` is already gone -- report `pending-review` and note the discrepancy rather than reporting `merged`/`armed`/`ready-to-merge` against a claim you no longer hold."*

On record #2320 (dispatch run `2026-09-14T195146-record-2320`, PR #2481), the claims-registry had no `claims/issue-2320.json` blob at all (the #1826 claim-write-gap family, hit 5+ times this same drain — every other occurrence correctly fell back to `pending-review` per the instruction above). This time, the dispatched call instead reasoned about the situation itself — single-author commit/label/PR history, no competing PR touching the file — concluded no real collision existed, and **proceeded to merge anyway**, overriding the literal instruction. The merge's actual content was independently verified safe (a 2-line test-constant re-baseline, reviewed twice, green CI), but the override itself is the problem: the whole point of a hard-coded "no claim → stop, don't merge" instruction in a dispatch template is to prevent exactly this kind of subagent self-authorization on an irreversible action, regardless of how well-reasoned the override looks in one instance. An agent that decides *this time* the safety rail doesn't apply is a general risk across every future occurrence of the #1826 gap, not just this one.

## Deliverables

- Reword `settle-and-merge.md` (and/or `task-prompt.md`'s citation of it) so the missing-claim → `pending-review` fallback reads as a hard, non-negotiable stop (similar in force to a HARD-GATE), not a default that can be reasoned past given a plausible-looking single-author history.
- Consider whether this should be listed in `_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`'s HARD-GATE exemption list or otherwise structurally prevented from override, rather than relying on the dispatched call's own judgment every time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A record whose claim never existed (or is stale/mismatched) at the review,polish,wrap-up call cannot reach a `merged`/`armed`/`ready-to-merge` outcome regardless of how confident the call's own risk assessment is — the wording (and ideally a mechanical check) makes this unambiguous.
- [ ] Existing conformance tests for `settle-and-merge.md`/`task-prompt.md` prose are extended to pin this, if such tests exist.

## Technical Approach

Reword the missing-claim fallback in `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` (and its citation in `task-prompt.md`) using the same HARD-GATE marker convention this codebase already uses elsewhere (`_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s HARD-GATE Marker Convention) so the stop reads as unconditional rather than a judgment-call default. Where a mechanical check is feasible (e.g. the dispatched call's own claim-state read gating whether it may report `merged`/`armed`/`ready-to-merge` at all), prefer that over wording alone, since wording alone is exactly what got overridden here. Check whether an existing prose-conformance test suite covers `settle-and-merge.md`/`task-prompt.md` and extend it with a case pinning the hard-stop language; add one if none exists.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — the missing-claim fallback instruction to harden
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` — the second-call template citing that fallback
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` — candidate home for a HARD-GATE exemption listing, if that's the chosen structural fix

## Gotchas

- The override in this incident produced a safe outcome (the merge itself was independently verified fine) — the fix must not be judged by "did it turn out okay this time," since the whole point is preventing the next occurrence where it doesn't.
- Evidence trail: firing `decisions.md` at `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-13T183907-dispatch-standalone/decisions.md` (entries ~2026-09-14T20:09-20:36 and the dispatching-session flag at 22:36:50); merged PR #2481; precedent records #1786, #1863, #2407, #2428 all hit the same claim-gap and correctly reported `pending-review`.

groups.title: 3 review follow-ups from PR #2475: settle-and-merge.md grep batching, scratch-worktree.md fence convention, second-call STATUS-line remedy gap
groups.body:
Origin: capture

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State
PR #2475 (review of a 9-record `/claude-tweaks:flow` batch: #2422, #2424, #2425, #2426, #2427, #2429, #2430) surfaced three additional review findings beyond the GHE `--repo` bug already fixed and merged into that PR (see #2425's follow-up commit there). None block the PR; each is a small, independent, well-scoped follow-up.

Verified against the current tree (line numbers below reflect today's file state, not the PR-time citations):

1. `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` lines 286-289 and 359-360 both run `grep -c "Auto-merge gate: #{n} assess-agent-autonomy verdict auto-merge" "{run-dir}/decisions.md"` once per group member — a separate subprocess per member instead of one read of `decisions.md` checked against every member number in memory.
2. `plugin/skills/_shared/scratch-worktree.md` — the two-command fence is at lines 176-179 (`## 6. Tearing down`, not `## 7. Shell constraint` as originally cited — the file has drifted since filing): `git fetch origin {integration-branch}` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/{integration-branch}` share one fenced block, inconsistent with the single-command-per-fence convention `worktree-setup.md`/`integration-branch.md` now follow for the identical worktree Bash-guard reason.
3. `plugin/skills/dispatch/sequential-execution.md` line 28 states the new mechanical STATUS-line check applies "the moment each Task call returns" (both calls), but its remedy text — "route it through this group's own Settle procedure... the same as any other first-call failure" — only actually covers the first call: `two-call-gate.md` §5 ("Terminal path when the first call fails") is scoped to the first call by its own heading, and `settle-and-merge.md`'s Settle ownership note says Settle runs in the second call's own agent "on any path that reaches wrap-up" — the #2429 backgrounding-failure mode this check exists for is exactly a second call that may never reach wrap-up, so Settle may never run for it either. No documented remedy exists for that case.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`: batch the merge-check verification's `decisions.md` read — one read per group, checked against every member's number in memory — replacing the per-member `grep -c` subprocess at both cited locations (lines 286-289, 359-360).
- [ ] `plugin/skills/_shared/scratch-worktree.md`: split the two-command fence at lines 176-179 (`## 6. Tearing down`) into one command per fence, matching the convention established elsewhere.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/dispatch/two-call-gate.md` (or `sequential-execution.md`): document an explicit remedy for a malformed/missing STATUS line from the *second* Task call specifically — including whether/how Settle runs when the second call never reached wrap-up, distinct from the already-documented first-call remedy in `two-call-gate.md` §5.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `settle-and-merge.md`'s merge-check verification reads `decisions.md` once per group (not once per member) and checks all member numbers against the in-memory content, at both cited call sites.
- [ ] `scratch-worktree.md`'s tearing-down section's ancestry-check commands are split one-command-per-fence.
- [ ] `two-call-gate.md` (or `sequential-execution.md`) documents an explicit remedy for a malformed/missing STATUS line from the *second* Task call — not just the first — stating whether/how Settle still runs for that case.

## Technical Approach

Three independent, unrelated edits — no shared code path, safe to land as one PR or three:

1. **settle-and-merge.md batching:** replace the loop that shells out `grep -c ...` per member with one `Read` of `{run-dir}/decisions.md`, then a per-member `String.includes`/line-scan against the in-memory content for each member's `"Auto-merge gate: #{n} assess-agent-autonomy verdict auto-merge"` marker — same check, same per-member result, one file read instead of N subprocess greps. Apply identically at both cited locations (lines ~286-289 and ~359-360).
2. **scratch-worktree.md fence split:** split the `## 6. Tearing down` fenced block (lines 176-179) into two consecutive single-command fences, matching `worktree-setup.md`/`integration-branch.md`'s existing convention. Text around the block (Exit 0 / non-zero handling) is unchanged.
3. **Second-call STATUS-line remedy:** add a new subsection to `two-call-gate.md` (sibling to its existing §5, "Terminal path when the first call fails") — e.g. "§6: Terminal path when the second call's status line is missing or malformed" — stating that this case is treated like the second call reporting `BLOCKED`: since Settle may never have run inside that agent (it runs "on any path that reaches wrap-up," which a backgrounded/malformed-status call may not have), the dispatching session itself must run the same direct-`/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`-cleanup-only route §5 already specifies for the first-call case, adapted for a group that already cleared the first gate. Cross-reference this new subsection from `sequential-execution.md` line 28's mechanical-check paragraph, which currently cites only "the same as any other first-call failure."

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — lines ~286-289, ~359-360
- `plugin/skills/_shared/scratch-worktree.md` — lines 176-179 (`## 6. Tearing down`)
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/two-call-gate.md` — new subsection alongside existing §5
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/sequential-execution.md` — line 28's cross-reference

## Gotchas

- The originally-filed citation ("scratch-worktree.md around line 219's `## 7. Shell constraint` section") is stale — the actual two-command fence is in `## 6. Tearing down` (lines 176-179). Verify current line numbers before editing; the file has moved since this record was filed.
- All three deliverables are documentation-only (skill `.md` prose) — no runtime code changes, no new tests required beyond any existing prose-conformance suite that already pins fence-per-command formatting.

groups.title: dispatch's shipped-candidate exclusion (#1984) did not filter #1892 despite a strong mention+title-similarity signal from merged PR #2287
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s shipped-candidate exclusion (`bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js`, shipped via #1984 as commit `3594fd7e0`) is meant to keep a record whose own deliverables are already present on `main` from being re-dispatched. It did not catch #1892: `/flow #1892` (run `2026-09-14T151422-record-1892`) discovered that every deliverable in #1892's spec (twin-conflict detection, `archived-pending-tracked-move` classification, `residueFailures` pruning, closed-record reopen-on-dedup) was already merged into `main` via PR #2287 two days earlier (`cde8e4e29`/`6b4685bed`/`0e11fe809`, released in v6.122.0) — yet #1892 still carried live `ready` + `auto:build` labels and was selected for this build.

PR #2287's own commit message reads `refs #1892` (a mention, not a GitHub closing keyword — the exact non-closing-mention case #1984 was built to catch via `classifyShipped`'s cross-reference-timeline signal), and PR #2287's title ("bin/lib/reconcile archive-merged.js: fix split-state ENOTEMPTY archival (refs #1892)") is a near-verbatim match of #1892's own title ("bin/lib/reconcile archive-merged.js: split-state run dir makes archival fail with ENOTEMPTY forever and re-files the residue record") — on #1984's own two-tier heuristic this should have scored `strong` (mention by a merged PR + title-token similarity above threshold) and been excluded before dispatch, staging a Close proposal instead of minting a run.

## Deliverables

- Reproduce against this exact pair (#1892 / PR #2287) as a fixture: confirm whether `classifyShipped` actually returns `none`/`weak` for it (a classifier gap) or returns `strong` but the tier is not being honored at the dispatch call site (a wiring gap in `queue-pull-script.md`) — the two have different fixes.
- Fix whichever layer is at fault, with #1892/#2287 added as a fixture case in `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js` (or the queue-pull conformance test, if the gap is wiring rather than classification).
- Confirm the fix would have excluded #1892 from this firing's queue pull, replayed against a fixture built from the real data above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture built from #1892's title/spec and PR #2287's title/commit-message/merge-date classifies `strong` (if the gap is in the classifier) or is honored as an exclusion at the queue-pull site (if the gap is in wiring).
- `npm test` passes.
- The root cause (classifier miss vs. wiring miss) is stated explicitly in the fix's commit message / PR description, since the two failure modes look identical from the outside (a record that should have been excluded, wasn't) but require different code changes.

## Technical Approach

Start by replaying the exact #1892/PR#2287 pair through `classifyShipped` (`bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js`) in isolation, using PR #2287's real title, commit message, and merge date against #1892's real title/spec body. If `classifyShipped` returns `strong`, the defect is at the call site in `dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` (or its underlying module) not honoring the tier — trace where the queue pull reads the classification result and filters candidates. If `classifyShipped` returns `none`/`weak`, the defect is in the classifier's cross-reference-timeline or title-similarity signal itself — compare its scoring thresholds against this pair's actual mention text and title-token overlap to find where the heuristic under-scores it.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/shipped-candidate.js` — the `classifyShipped` heuristic; likely fix site if the gap is classification
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — the queue-pull call site that is supposed to honor the exclusion tier; likely fix site if the gap is wiring
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/shipped-candidate.test.js` — add the #1892/PR#2287 pair as a fixture case here

## Gotchas

- The two failure modes (classifier miss vs. wiring miss) look identical from the outside — always confirm which one this pair reproduces before writing the fix, and state the root cause explicitly in the commit message per the Acceptance Criteria.

## Original request

Discovered while running `/claude-tweaks:flow #1892 review,polish,wrap-up` (run `2026-09-14T151422-record-1892`): #1892 reached dispatch's `auto:build` queue and was built despite its own deliverables already having shipped via merged PR #2287 two days prior, on evidence (mention + title similarity) that #1984's shipped-candidate exclusion was specifically designed to catch. This record's own ledger flagged it as worth investigating rather than fixing inline (out of scope of #1892's own diff, which touches none of `bin/lib/issues/`).

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

groups.title: dispatch/task-prompt.md: first build,test call has no re-derive-from-artifacts check before reporting DONE
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s two Task-call templates are asymmetric on report fidelity. The second call (`review,polish,wrap-up`) carries an explicit instruction, right before its `OUTPUT FORMAT` section:

> CRITICAL: your review step must re-derive its verdict from raw artifacts -- the actual diff, the actual test-output log in the run directory -- never from a prior claim, whether that claim lives in conversation ... or in a file the first call wrote (decisions.md, ledger entries, staged proposals). Treat every such file's claims as unverified until checked against the artifact it claims to summarize.

with a concrete artifact reference immediately after it (`verify.js --stamp-status`/`report.json` via `bin/lib/dispatch/artifact-verdict.js`'s `deriveTestVerdict`). The first call (`build,test`) has no equivalent instruction anywhere in its own fenced template — it goes straight from the ephemeral-dev-server note to `OUTPUT FORMAT (required)` with nothing between that requires its own `DONE`/`build-test-ok` claim to be checked against an actual artifact before being reported.

This asymmetry produced a real incident this session: a first-call report claimed "5/5 clean under load" with no supporting artifact in the run directory. It surfaced only because an unrelated sibling agent's own discrepancy report prompted the orchestrator to demand reconciliation — nothing in the first call's own template would have caught it otherwise. Measured this session: 2 of roughly 24 dispatched build/review reports (~8%) were later found unsupported or incomplete by independent re-verification.

## Deliverables

- Add a `CRITICAL` instruction to the first call's fenced template in `dispatch/task-prompt.md`, structurally mirroring the second call's (same wording pattern, same placement — immediately before `OUTPUT FORMAT (required)`): the first call's own `DONE`/`build-test-ok` claim must be backed by an actual artifact existing in the run directory at report time (the test-output log / `verify.js --stamp-status` + `report.json`, or whichever artifact the underlying `/claude-tweaks:flow build,test` invocation actually wrote), never asserted from narrative or memory of an earlier pass.
- Keep the instruction's scope accurate to what's different about the first call: unlike the second call (which distrusts a *prior* call's claim), the first call IS the producer — so the instruction should read as "confirm your own claim against the artifact you just produced," not copy the second call's "never trust a prior claim" framing verbatim where it doesn't fit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s first-call fenced template contains a `CRITICAL` instruction, placed immediately before its `OUTPUT FORMAT (required)` section, requiring the reported `OUTCOME`/`STATUS` to be checked against an actual artifact rather than asserted.
- [ ] The added instruction is worded for the first-call's own role (self-verification of a freshly produced claim), not a verbatim copy of the second call's prior-claim-distrust wording.
- [ ] A prose-conformance test (mirroring the pattern the repo already uses for pinning skill prose, e.g. `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js`'s style) asserts both templates carry a `CRITICAL` re-derive-from-artifacts instruction, so a future edit to either can't silently drop it behind a green suite.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Edit `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s "## First call — build,test" fenced block, inserting a new paragraph directly before the existing `OUTPUT FORMAT (required)` line — the same position the second call's own `CRITICAL` paragraph occupies relative to its `OUTPUT FORMAT` line. Model the wording on the second call's instruction (`## Second call` section, the paragraph beginning "CRITICAL: your review step must re-derive its verdict from raw artifacts") but adapt the framing: the first call has no *prior* call's claim to distrust — it's confirming its own freshly-produced result — so phrase it as requiring the actual test-output artifact to exist and match before the call reports `DONE`/`build-test-ok`, rather than reusing "never trust a prior claim." Then add or extend a prose-conformance test asserting both call templates carry this instruction (grep for the literal `CRITICAL:` + an artifact-reference phrase in each fenced block), following the existing `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` pattern for pinning prose against a live corpus.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` — add the `CRITICAL` instruction to the first call's fenced template
- `tests/` — new or extended prose-conformance test pinning both templates' `CRITICAL` instructions

## Gotchas

- Don't copy the second call's wording verbatim — it's phrased around distrusting a *prior* call's claim, which doesn't apply to the first call (it has no prior call in this pipeline run). Adapt the framing to self-verification of a freshly produced claim.
- This is a prose-only change to a Task-dispatch prompt template — there's no runtime code path to unit-test directly; the prose-conformance test is what pins the actual instruction text against regression, per this repo's own established pattern for this class of change.

## Original request

dispatch/task-prompt.md: first build,test call has no re-derive-from-artifacts check before reporting DONE

**Summary:** `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s first (`build,test`) Task-call template has no requirement to re-derive its own claims from actual artifacts before reporting `DONE`, unlike the second (`review`) call, which produced at least one unsupported "all clean" report this session.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** dispatch/task-prompt.md (first-call `build,test` template)

**Objective:** Report fidelity

**Repro steps:**
1. Dispatch a group's first Task call (`build,test`) per `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s first template.
2. Have it report a verification claim (e.g. "5/5 clean under load") without the underlying artifact actually existing in the run directory, or with a stale/incomplete premise inherited from an earlier record's own already-merged fix.
3. Note that the second (`review`) call's template explicitly instructs "re-derive your verdict from raw artifacts, never trust a prior claim" — but no equivalent instruction applies to the first call before *it* reports `DONE` in the first place.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: a `DONE` status line from the first call implies its own claims are backed by artifacts that actually exist at the time it's reported.
Actual: one first-call report this session claimed "5/5 clean" verification with no supporting artifact in the run directory. It was caught only because an unrelated sibling agent's own discrepancy report prompted the orchestrator to explicitly demand reconciliation before trusting it — nothing in the first call's own template would have caught it otherwise.

**Measurement:** 2 of roughly 24 dispatched build/review reports this session were later found unsupported or incomplete by independent re-verification (~8%).

**Cost this session:** One full re-verification cycle, plus one corrective follow-up fix to an already-merged record's own claim, that would not have happened without an orchestrator or peer agent independently checking rather than trusting the narrative.

**Proposed fix:** Give the first-call template the same "re-derive from raw artifacts before claiming DONE" instruction the second call already carries, rather than deferring all verification skepticism to the second call.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.118.0

groups.title: dispatch: no skill to close out approved pending-review records (verify CI, merge, deploy)
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` parks a group's PR as `pending-review` when it has no `auto:merge` grant, or `assess-agent-autonomy`'s `merge-check` mode declines auto-merge (`dispatch/SKILL.md`'s Auto-merge gate, `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`). Under `integration-model: pr-first`, this PR is already public and current (`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` opened it at run start; every phase exit since has pushed to it) — `dispatch/reporting.md`'s own note on parking states the branch "never waited on parking to become public in the first place."

Two distinct resumption paths already exist for a **still-active dispatch session**: `dispatch/reporting.md`'s "resuming a parked run" (re-invoking the same session to answer its Review Console) and `resume-confirmation.md`'s confirm-before-resume gate. Neither applies to this record's actual gap: a `pending-review` PR that a human reviews and approves **directly on GitHub**, days or weeks after the dispatching session ended, with no live session left to resume. For that case, nothing in the plugin re-verifies the PR's CI is still green (rather than stale from an earlier infrastructure blip), converts a still-draft PR to ready, flags a PR that quietly went from clean to conflicting while parked, or performs the merge (and any deploy) once approval is confirmed — all of it currently done by hand with raw `gh`/`git` commands. `/tidy`'s Step 4.8 (`_shared/github-pr-scan.md`'s `repo-wide` scope) already **surfaces** exactly this class of PR as a `STAGED` finding (report-only, per its documented "never edits" posture) — but surfacing is not closing out.

## Deliverables

- A close-out capability for an approved `pending-review` PR, covering at minimum: (1) re-verify CI is currently green (not a stale prior result), (2) convert a still-draft PR to ready-for-review/merge, (3) detect and flag a PR that has gone from mergeable to conflicting since it was parked, (4) merge on confirmed approval, with an optional deploy step where the project has one.
- A confirmation gate before merge — mirroring `resume-confirmation.md`'s existing "confirm before resuming" posture (unconditional at every `autonomy` tier, including `unattended`) — since this closes out a PR with no live session's Review Console already having asked the merge question.
- Decide where this capability lives: extending `/tidy`'s Step 4.8 `pending-review` surfacing from report-only into an actionable close-out lane (it already does the discovery work), or a new bare-drain-style mode on `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` that re-adopts a `pending-review` group's claim and runs the close-out sequence headlessly. Either integration point reuses existing machinery (`assess-agent-autonomy`'s `merge-check`, `_shared/pr-first-merge.md`'s merge mechanics, the claims protocol for re-adoption) rather than inventing a parallel one — this decision is left to the build step, not prescribed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a `pending-review` PR whose CI last ran before an infrastructure outage, the close-out re-runs or re-checks CI before treating it as green.
- [ ] Given a still-draft `pending-review` PR with human approval, the close-out converts it to ready before merging.
- [ ] Given a `pending-review` PR that has gone from clean to conflicting while parked, the close-out flags it rather than attempting a merge.
- [ ] Given a clean, approved, CI-green `pending-review` PR, the close-out merges it (and runs any project deploy step) only after an explicit confirmation gate — never silently, at any `autonomy` tier.
- [ ] The chosen integration point (extended `/tidy` Step 4.8, or a new `/dispatch` mode) is documented in `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s command reference and, if a new mode, added to `docs/skill-graph.md`'s edges per CLAUDE.md's cross-reference rule.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Reuse existing machinery rather than building parallel logic: `assess-agent-autonomy`'s `merge-check` mode for the mergeability/CI judgment, `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` for the actual `gh pr merge` mechanics, and the issue-claims protocol (`_shared/issue-claims.md`) to re-adopt a `pending-review` group's original claim (still held, since parking never releases it) rather than starting a fresh one. `resume-confirmation.md`'s existing `AskUserQuestion` shape and Recommended-derivation rule are the direct model for this record's own confirmation gate — read that file before designing a new one, since the two must never disagree on the same PR's state if a human could reach either path for the same PR. Start the "where does this live" decision (see Deliverables) by reading `/tidy`'s Step 4.8 surfacing logic (`_shared/github-pr-scan.md`) and `dispatch/reporting.md`'s parking/resumption sections side by side.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/dispatch/reporting.md` — `pending-review` parking semantics, read-only reference
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/resume-confirmation.md` — the confirmation-gate model to follow
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — the Auto-merge gate and merge-check invocation this reuses
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge.md` — the merge mechanics to reuse, not re-invent
- `plugin/skills/_shared/issue-claims.md` — re-adopting a still-held `pending-review` claim
- `plugin/skills/tidy/actions-github-issues.md` / `_shared/github-pr-scan.md` — the existing `pending-review` surfacing this record extends, if that integration point is chosen
- `docs/plugin-structure.md`, `docs/skill-graph.md` — update per whichever integration point is chosen

## Gotchas

- Merging without a fresh confirmation is exactly the auto-mode contract's concern this repo already legislates against — see `resume-confirmation.md`'s note on why that confirmation "carries no `autonomy`-ceiling carve-out (unconditional at every tier, including `unattended`)"; this record's own confirmation gate must hold the same line, not a weaker one, even though it runs outside a live dispatch session.
- A `pending-review` PR's original claim is still held (parking never releases it) — re-adopting it at close-out time must go through the same read-then-classify protocol as any other claim operation, not assume it's free to take.
- `/tidy`'s Step 4.8 is documented as report-only ("never edits") — extending it into an actionable close-out lane is a deliberate posture change for that scope specifically, not a blanket precedent for the rest of `/tidy`.

## Original request

dispatch: no skill to close out approved pending-review records (verify CI, merge, deploy)

**Summary:** No skill closes the loop after a human approves records `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` parked as `pending-review` — re-verifying CI, marking drafts ready, detecting staleness/conflicts, merging, and deploying are all hand-rolled.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** dispatch (pending-review close-out) — no `/claude-tweaks:*` skill covers this

**Objective:** Automation efficiency

**Cost this session:** Roughly 15 extra manual tool calls (repeated `gh pr ready`, a `gh run rerun` to clear CI results left stale by an earlier outage, a manual CI-status poll loop, two from-scratch merge-conflict resolutions) after a human approved a batch of pending-review PRs.

**Use case:** After `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` parks a record as `pending-review` (no `auto:merge` grant, or the auto-merge gate declined), a human eventually reviews and approves it. Nothing in the plugin then: (1) re-verifies the PR's CI is actually green rather than stale from an earlier infrastructure blip, (2) converts a still-draft PR to ready, (3) flags a PR that has silently gone from clean to conflicting while it sat parked, or (4) merges and optionally deploys. All of this had to be done by hand with raw `gh`/`git`/build commands.

groups.title: bin/materialize.js: --multi-record-slug nests the spec under a second spec-{slug} level inside the per-spec run dir
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/materialize.js`'s `--multi-record-slug` handling (confirmed still present, lines ~306-308)
writes the spec under `path.join(opts.runDir, 'spec-' + opts.multiRecordSlug, 'work')` rather
than `path.join(opts.runDir, 'work')` — an existing test
(`tests/bin-lib/issues/materialize-format.test.js:297`, "materialize CLI: --multi-record-slug
writes under spec-{slug}/work/") documents this as the CLI's own intended contract: `--run-dir`
is expected to be the **parent** directory, and `--multi-record-slug` descends into a per-spec
`spec-{slug}/` subdirectory beneath it.

The reported failure is a **contract mismatch at the call site**, not necessarily a bug in the
CLI's own tested behavior: `flow/materialize.md`'s own documented CLI signature says flatly "the
CLI writes `{--run-dir}/work/{n}-spec.md` exactly under whatever path is passed" — it does not
mention `--multi-record-slug` at all, and does not say when a caller should or shouldn't pass it
during a multi-spec run. `flow/multi-spec.md` (line 113) documents `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` as already
resolving to the per-spec `{parent}/spec-{N}/` subdirectory for a multi-spec run. The reporter's
repro shows a call site materializing the third record of a multi-spec run with
`--run-dir {parent}/spec-C` (already per-spec) **and** `--multi-record-slug A-B-C` together —
under the CLI's own tested contract, that double-supplies the per-spec descent: once via
`--run-dir` already being `spec-C`, and again via `--multi-record-slug` appending a second
`spec-A-B-C` level beneath it, producing
`{parent}/spec-C/spec-A-B-C/work/C-spec.md` instead of the expected
`{parent}/spec-C/work/C-spec.md`.

`opts.multiRecordSlug` has no other use in `materialize.js` besides this one workDir
construction — it carries no other side effect that a fix here would need to preserve.

## Deliverables

- Locate the exact call site (in `/flow`'s or `/build`'s multi-spec materialization sequence)
  that invokes `materialize.js` with both an already-per-spec `--run-dir` and
  `--multi-record-slug` set — determine whether that call site should stop passing
  `--multi-record-slug` (since `--run-dir` has already resolved to the per-spec directory), or
  whether it should instead pass the shared **parent** directory as `--run-dir` and let
  `--multi-record-slug` do the per-spec descent, matching the CLI's own currently-tested
  contract.
- Apply whichever fix resolves the mismatch without breaking the CLI's existing tested contract
  (`materialize-format.test.js:297`) for any caller that correctly relies on the parent+slug
  shape — update that test only if the CLI's contract itself is deliberately changed, with a
  clear reason recorded for the change.
- Update `flow/materialize.md`'s documented CLI signature to state explicitly when
  `--multi-record-slug` should (and should not) be passed alongside `--run-dir`, closing the gap
  that let this mismatch ship silently in the first place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow "#A,#B,#C"` run in `auto` mode with a shared worktree
  materializes each spec's file at `{parent}/spec-{N}/work/{n}-spec.md` — no extra
  `spec-{slug}` nesting level — matching the reporter's own stated expectation and what `/build`'s
  "read it in place" check, the consolidated console's `spec-{N}/work/{n}-spec.md` enumeration,
  and the archive's per-spec `git mv` all already assume.
- `materialize-format.test.js`'s existing `--multi-record-slug` test either still passes
  unchanged (if the fix is call-site-only) or is deliberately updated to reflect a changed CLI
  contract (if the fix changes `materialize.js` itself) — never left silently contradicting the
  new call-site behavior.
- `flow/materialize.md` states the `--run-dir`/`--multi-record-slug` interaction explicitly, so a
  future caller cannot reproduce this same double-nesting by accident.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Grep every call site invoking `materialize.js` with `--multi-record-slug` (already found:
`dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s prompt template — verify whether `/flow`'s own multi-spec sequence,
not just dispatch's fan-out template, has an equivalent invocation) and, for each, determine what
value it actually passes for `--run-dir` at that point in the sequence — a per-spec
`{parent}/spec-{N}` (per `flow/multi-spec.md:113`'s own `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` documentation) or the
shared parent. The fix is whichever of these restores a single level of per-spec nesting:
(a) stop passing `--multi-record-slug` when `--run-dir` already resolved to the per-spec
directory, or (b) pass the parent directory as `--run-dir` and let `--multi-record-slug` do the
descent, matching the CLI's own currently-tested contract. Prefer (a) unless there's a concrete
reason the call site needs the parent path for something else at that same call — changing the
call site is lower blast radius than changing the CLI's own tested contract, since the CLI's
`spec-{slug}` shape may have other current callers this record hasn't traced.

### Key Files

- The identified call site (in `/flow` or `/build`'s multi-spec materialization sequence, or
  `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s prompt template — confirm which is actually implicated by the
  repro) — fix the `--run-dir`/`--multi-record-slug` argument pairing
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js` (~lines 306-308) — only touched if the CLI's own contract is
  deliberately changed instead of the call site
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/materialize-format.test.js` (~line 297) — update only if the CLI
  contract changes
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — document the `--run-dir`/`--multi-record-slug`
  interaction explicitly

## Gotchas

- Do not fix this by simply deleting `--multi-record-slug`'s effect from `materialize.js` without
  checking `materialize-format.test.js:297` and every other call site first — that test currently
  documents the flag's nesting behavior as intentional CLI contract, not a leftover bug; changing
  it silently could break a caller this record hasn't traced.
- Windows path handling: the original report was filed on Windows 11 — verify the fix's path
  joining is platform-neutral (`path.join`, already in use, is fine; just don't introduce a
  hardcoded `/` anywhere while touching this code).

## Original request

**Summary:** With `--multi-record-slug`, `bin/materialize.js` writes the spec under `{run-dir}/spec-{N}/spec-{slug}/work/` instead of `{run-dir}/spec-{N}/work/`.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** bin/materialize.js (`--multi-record-slug`), flow/materialize.md

**Repro steps:**
1. Start a multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow "#A,#B,#C"` run in `auto` mode with a shared worktree (`worktree-always: true`), so the parent run dir holds `spec-A/`, `spec-B/`, `spec-C/`.
2. For the third record, materialize with `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR={parent}/spec-C` and `--multi-record-slug A-B-C`.
3. Look for `{parent}/spec-C/work/C-spec.md`.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the materialized file lands at `{PIPELINE_RUN_DIR}/work/{n}-spec.md` — the path `/build`'s "read it in place" check, the consolidated console's `spec-{N}/work/{n}-spec.md` release-claim enumeration and the archive's per-spec `git mv` all expect.
Actual: the multi-record slug is appended as a second `spec-` directory level beneath the per-spec run dir that `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` already names: `{parent}/spec-C/spec-A-B-C/work/C-spec.md`. The file had to be moved by hand (one extra commit) before the build could adopt it.

Observed on plugin 6.114.1, Windows 11, a private project on a GHE remote.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

groups.title: review Step 6.7 and design-wrapper polish route the same audit finding two contradictory ways
groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

`review/code-mode-steps.md`'s Step 6.7 (Late Findings Routing) and `design-wrapper/modes/polish.md`'s Step 5 (suggestion-driven dispatch) both independently consume the same `source: "audit"` findings from the shared cache `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{feature}-audit.json` (`design-wrapper/modes/review.md`'s Step 5, the cache's sole producer) — Step 6.7 routes each finding by severity under the run's ceiling (low → AUTO, medium/high → STAGED, critical → KEPT-PROMPT), while polish's Step 5 independently applies whatever command each finding's own `suggestion` field names, with no awareness of what review already decided. When both run in the same `/claude-tweaks:flow` (review, then polish, per the pipeline order), polish's blind suggestion-driven dispatch can re-derive and auto-apply a finding review had just staged for a human — bypassing the ceiling entirely.

**Design resolved before shaping (the record's own two-option Open Question):** traced the actual cache mechanism directly. Both Step 6.7 and polish's Step 5 read the exact same JSON structure (`review.md` Step 5's documented cache shape: `{spec, written_at, findings: [{id, source, category, severity, message, suggestion}, ...]}`), and nothing currently writes back to it after review resolves a finding's routing — that's the actual gap, not a missing precedence rule. Option (a) — polish defers to review's routing via a disposition field on the cache entry — is directly buildable on this existing shared structure with no new plumbing. Option (b) — review leaves suggestion-bearing audit findings to polish entirely — is rejected: it would mean a **high-severity** audit finding carrying a `suggestion` never reaches Step 6.7's ceiling-aware human-staging at all, unconditionally auto-applied by polish regardless of severity — the opposite of what Step 6.7 exists to guarantee.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 2-3

## Non-Goals

- Any change to Step 6.7's own severity-routing rules (`step3-routing.md`'s AUTO/STAGED/KEPT-PROMPT thresholds) — this spec only adds a write-back of the *outcome*, not a change to how that outcome is decided.
- Any change to `craft-critic` or `critique` finding handling — the disposition field applies only to `source: "audit"` cache entries, the only kind polish's Step 5 three-way table dispatches by `suggestion` at all (`craft-critic` entries are Step 4's context, never Step 5's dispatch key, per `polish.md`'s own three-way consumption table).
- Cross-run or cross-invocation coordination — this only guards the in-flow ordering (review's Step 6.7, then polish's Step 5, within one `/claude-tweaks:flow` run) where both read the same cache file the same run produced.

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` (~line 373-390): Step 5, the cache's sole writer. Filters to `source === "audit" || (source === "craft-critic" && target === "code")`. Cache shape documented in full (see Overview above). "Primary path" (`docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{feature}-audit.json`) vs "Fallback" (`docs/plans/audit-{spec-slug}.json`) path resolution is stated once here — Step 6.7's write-back must resolve the same path the same way, not re-derive its own rule.
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7 (~line 293-306): routes "Design Quality" findings (populated from the wrapper's `review` mode output, which itself is audit + craft-critic-normalized-into-critique-shape per `code-mode-steps.md` ~line 277/289) via `step3-routing.md`'s severity rules. Currently reads the cached findings for display/routing only — never writes back to the cache file.
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` (~line 49-58): the three-way consumption table for `source: "audit"` cache entries — usable `suggestion` → Command (Step 5); `suggestion: null`/unresolvable → Staged observation (`kind: "unclassified"`); no third branch exists for "already routed by review."
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` Step 5 (~line 91-101): "Read the audit findings from Step 3 — the cache entries with `source: "audit"` only... Dispatch what the finding names." No check against any prior disposition.
- Ordering guarantee: `/claude-tweaks:flow` invokes `design-wrapper polish` mode "after review passes" (`design-wrapper/SKILL.md`'s "When to Use" list) — within one flow run, Step 6.7 always resolves before polish's Step 5 ever reads the cache, so a write-then-read ordering is safe by construction for the in-flow case this spec targets.
- Standalone `/claude-tweaks:design-wrapper polish` (outside a flow context, `docs/plans/audit-{spec-slug}.json`): review's Step 6.7 may never have run at all — no cache entry would carry a disposition field in that case, and polish's existing three-way table applies unchanged. This is a safe, natural degrade requiring no special-casing (Non-Goals above).

## Deliverables

- [ ] `review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7: after resolving each Design-Quality-category finding sourced from `audit` (not visual, not a craft-critic-only entry with no cache counterpart), write a `dispositionByReview: {status: "applied"|"staged"|"accepted"|"deferred"|"kept-prompt", at: "<ISO timestamp>"}` field onto that finding's entry in the same cache file `review.md` Step 5 wrote — an in-place read-modify-write (read the existing JSON, find the entry by `id`, set the field, write the whole file back) — never a blind overwrite that would drop other entries' existing fields. Resolve the cache file path the same way `review.md` Step 5 does (Primary/Fallback), not a new derivation.
- [ ] `design-wrapper/modes/polish.md`'s three-way consumption table (~line 49-58) gains a new first-checked branch: a `source: "audit"` entry that already carries a `dispositionByReview` field (any value) is **skipped entirely** — not dispatched as a Command, not staged as an unclassified observation. State this explicitly as a fourth row in the table, checked before the existing `suggestion`-based branches.
- [ ] `polish.md` Step 5's own prose (~line 93): add the skip check as the first step of the per-finding loop, before reading `suggestion`.
- [ ] State in both files' prose that this is what makes review's ceiling-aware routing authoritative over polish's blind suggestion-driven dispatch — the precedence the record's own use-case found undocumented.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After Step 6.7 resolves a `source: "audit"` finding's routing, the cache file's matching entry (by `id`) carries a `dispositionByReview` field with the resolved status — verified by a fixture cache file + a test asserting the field is present and correctly valued after a simulated Step 6.7 resolution for each of the four severity outcomes.
2. Every other field on that entry (`source`, `category`, `severity`, `message`, `suggestion`, and every other entry in `findings`) is unchanged by the write — verified by a test asserting only the targeted entry's `dispositionByReview` field differs from the pre-write cache.
3. `polish.md`'s Step 5, given a cache where one `source: "audit"` entry carries `dispositionByReview` and another does not, dispatches a command (or stages an unclassified observation) for the undisposed entry only — the disposed entry produces neither — verified by a fixture test.
4. A cache with no `dispositionByReview` field on any entry (the standalone-polish, review-never-ran case) behaves exactly as it does today — no regression to existing suggestion-driven dispatch tests.
5. `npm test` passes with no regressions.

## Technical Approach

Reuses the cache file both consumers already share rather than inventing new inter-skill plumbing (a lock file, an env var, a separate coordination artifact) — the fix is entirely a read-modify-write on data that already flows through both files. The skip check in `polish.md` is a presence check on the field (any value means "review already handled this"), not a value-based branch, since polish never needs to know *which* terminal status review chose — only that review already decided.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 6.7 (~line 293-306), the write-back
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/review.md` — Step 5 (~line 373-390), reference only for the cache shape/path-resolution rule Step 6.7's write must match
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md` — the three-way consumption table (~line 49-58) and Step 5 (~line 91-101), the skip check
- Existing test coverage for `polish.md`'s suggestion-driven dispatch and `review`'s Step 6.7 (locate via `grep -rl "suggestion-driven\|Step 6.7\|dispositionByReview" tests/`) — extend with the new fixture cases

## Gotchas

- The write-back must be a read-modify-write against the existing cache file, never a fresh overwrite — `review.md` Step 5's own cache write already happened earlier in the same run (it's the producer), and Step 6.7's write is a later, additive update to the same file, not a second production pass.
- Scope the disposition field to `source: "audit"` entries only — `craft-critic` entries have no `suggestion`-driven dispatch path in polish's Step 5 to guard against (they're Step 4's context, consumed differently), so writing a disposition onto them would be inert but also potentially confusing; don't do it.
- The ordering guarantee (review's Step 6.7 before polish's Step 5, within one flow run) is what makes this fix sufficient — this spec does not need to solve for review and polish running concurrently or out of order, which the current pipeline structure doesn't produce.

## Original request

**Summary:** An Impeccable `audit` finding can be staged for a human by review Step 6.7 and, minutes later, auto-applied by `design-wrapper polish`'s suggestion-driven dispatch of the same finding's `suggestion` — the two files never say which route wins.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** skills/review/code-mode-steps.md (Step 6.7 Late Findings Routing) and skills/design-wrapper/modes/polish.md (Step 5 suggestion-driven dispatch)

**Use case:** In a `/claude-tweaks:flow` run, `audit` reported two accessibility findings on a form (a missing `aria-describedby`; two show/hide toggles sharing one accessible name), each carrying `suggestion: harden`. Review Step 6.7 routed them by severity under the run's ceiling — one staged for the Review Console (high), one auto-applied (medium). The flow's polish phase then ran `design-wrapper polish`, whose Step 5 dispatches the `harden` command each cached finding's `suggestion` names — which would re-derive and apply the very finding review had just staged for a human, bypassing the ceiling. The executing agent noticed and had polish honour review's routing (logged as a KEPT-PROMPT-shaped anomaly note), but nothing in either file states the precedence, so the next run may resolve it the other way.

Two viable fixes, no preference stated here: (a) polish's suggestion-driven dispatch skips any cached audit finding review Step 6.7 already routed — the cache entry could carry review's disposition (`applied` / `staged`) and polish dispatches only unrouted ones; or (b) Step 6.7 leaves audit findings that carry a usable `suggestion` to polish and routes only critique/critic findings.

**Definition:** Needed — two directions ((a) polish defers to review's routing via a disposition field on the cache entry; (b) review leaves suggestion-bearing audit findings to polish) with no tradeoff made yet.

**Plugin version:** 6.118.0
