groups.title: Audit CLAUDE.md files against Anthropic's own <200-line context-engineering guidance
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Anthropic's own context-engineering guidance says Claude Code's own system prompt was cut by over 80% for Opus 5/Fable 5 with no measurable eval loss, and targets CLAUDE.md files at roughly under 200 lines. An independent audit of a real 388-skill repository found its CLAUDE.md at 829 lines / 110KB — 4x over that target, with one section alone consuming 86,630 characters. A separate piece from the same author on writing a good global CLAUDE.md argues each rule should name a specific past failure rather than state vague preferences (e.g. "write clean code"). claude-tweaks generates and maintains CLAUDE.md content across projects with no check against this size or authoring guidance. Notably, this repo's own CLAUDE.md already practices a related discipline manually — its `## Don'ts` section states "Full rule list now lives in docs/donts.md (moved out of this always-loaded file to fit the 150-line budget)" — so a lint/audit check would formalize and enforce a budget this repo already tries to hold ad hoc.

## Deliverables

- A lint/audit check (as part of `/code-health` or a dedicated pass) that flags a project's CLAUDE.md when it exceeds roughly 200 lines or shows a single runaway section.
- Authoring guidance in claude-tweaks' own CLAUDE.md docs citing the <200-line target and the "name a specific failure, not a vague preference" principle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the check against a sample of enrolled repos' CLAUDE.md files reports a pass/fail against the line-count guidance.

## Technical Approach

Add a mechanical line-count + largest-section-size check, following the existing pattern of a `/code-health` or `harness-health` scan step (a metadata-only read: file path, line count, section boundaries via `##`/`###` heading scan — never reading full section prose into a report unless flagging it). Pair with a documentation addition to this repo's own `CLAUDE.md`-authoring guidance (likely `docs/skill-authoring.md` or wherever CLAUDE.md conventions are documented) citing the <200-line target and the specific-failure-not-vague-preference principle — this repo's own `claude-md-conciseness` convention (already referenced elsewhere in this codebase's memory/practice) is a natural place to extend rather than duplicate.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/code-health/` or `plugin/skills/harness-health/` — new lint/audit check for CLAUDE.md size
- `docs/skill-authoring.md` (or wherever CLAUDE.md-authoring guidance already lives) — the <200-line target + specific-failure principle

## Gotchas

- This repo's own CLAUDE.md is itself close to or over a strict 200-line reading depending on how the `docs/donts.md`/`docs/incident-log.md` extraction is counted — verify the check's own line-count definition (raw file lines vs. effective always-loaded content) before flagging this repo's own file as a false positive.
- "Roughly 200 lines" is Anthropic's stated target, not a hard requirement — the check should flag for review, not hard-fail a build; frame the pass/fail output as a signal, not a gate.

## Original request

Audit CLAUDE.md files against Anthropic's own <200-line context-engineering guidance

Current State:
- Anthropic's own context-engineering guidance (Thariq Shihipar, "The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models", claude.com/blog) says Claude Code's own system prompt was cut by over 80% for Opus 5/Fable 5 with no measurable eval loss, and targets CLAUDE.md files at roughly under 200 lines.
- An independent audit of a real 388-skill repository found its CLAUDE.md at 829 lines / 110KB -- 4x over that target, with one section alone consuming 86,630 characters.
- A separate piece from the same author on writing a good global CLAUDE.md argues each rule should name a specific past failure rather than state vague preferences (e.g. "write clean code").
- claude-tweaks generates and maintains CLAUDE.md content across projects with no check against this size or authoring guidance.

Deliverables:
- A lint/audit check (as part of code-health or a dedicated pass) that flags a project's CLAUDE.md when it exceeds roughly 200 lines or shows a single runaway section.
- Authoring guidance in claude-tweaks' own CLAUDE.md docs citing the <200-line target and the "name a specific failure, not a vague preference" principle.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running the check against a sample of enrolled repos' CLAUDE.md files reports a pass/fail against the line-count guidance.

Source: https://medium.com/@alirezarezvani/claude-code-context-engineering-78-of-my-claude-md-failed-the-audit-d59b6931463e , https://medium.com/@nitingavhane/top-10-things-to-install-after-you-first-open-claude-code-cut-your-first-day-friction-by-80-49ea3d5a2e87 , https://medium.com/@alirezarezvani/a-global-claude-md-and-its-best-pieces-972ba72b408e (citing Anthropic, "The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models")

groups.title: visual-review/discover-mode.md: migrate stale batch/snapshot/vitals syntax to Playwright CLI
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md` (line ~111) still describes an `agent-browser`-era `batch` invocation bundling `open`, `snapshot -i -c`, annotated `screenshot`, and `vitals` per page:

> "For each approved candidate, open a session and walk the candidate journey via a `batch` invocation that bundles `open`, `snapshot -i -c`, annotated `screenshot`, and `vitals` per page (same shape as the worked example in `journey-mode.md`)."

This is now-broken syntax under Playwright CLI, which has no `batch` command. The 5-part playwright-cli-consumer-migration (#2645-#2649) excluded this reference because its automated check only matched lines carrying the literal string "agent-browser" — `discover-mode.md`'s line doesn't name `agent-browser` explicitly, so the migration's sweep missed it even though the syntax it describes (`batch`, `snapshot -i -c`) is exactly the pre-migration form.

Sibling records already resolved both underlying gaps that this line touches:
- **`batch`**: #2646/#2647 confirmed no Playwright CLI equivalent exists; the established replacement pattern is a sequence of individual commands against the same `-s=<name>` session (see `journey-mode.md`'s "Assemble the sequence" section, lines ~19-33, including its worked example of three sequential `open`/`snapshot`/`screenshot`/`goto` commands ending in `close`).
- **`vitals`**: #2647 confirmed no Playwright CLI equivalent exists; the established pattern is to omit the vitals capture step and note the capability gap in place (see `journey-mode.md` lines ~21-22, `page-mode.md` lines ~19-20, and `browser-review.md` line ~136).

`discover-mode.md`'s Phase 3 walk section (lines ~111-118) needs the same treatment `journey-mode.md` already received, reusing its already-established sequential-command pattern rather than inventing a new one.

## Deliverables
1. Replace `discover-mode.md`'s line ~111 `batch` invocation description with a sequence of individual `playwright-cli` commands (`open`/`goto`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`) against one named session, following the exact pattern `journey-mode.md`'s "Assemble the sequence" section already establishes (including its worked-example command block style).
2. Remove or replace the `vitals` reference in the same line and in the numbered walk steps below it (lines ~113-118, e.g. "snapshot + annotated screenshot + vitals" in step 4) per the same vitals-capability-gap note pattern `journey-mode.md`/`page-mode.md`/`browser-review.md` already use — omit the capture, add an in-place capability-gap comment/note rather than silently dropping the mention.
3. Update the numbered walk steps (lines ~113-118) that reference "the batched output" to instead describe reviewing the sequential command output, consistent with how `journey-mode.md`'s "Per-step review" section (line ~40) already frames it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `discover-mode.md` no longer describes a `batch` invocation anywhere in its Phase 3 walk section — the section instead describes a sequence of individual `playwright-cli` commands, matching `journey-mode.md`'s established pattern.
- `discover-mode.md`'s walk steps no longer instruct the reader to capture or review `vitals` output as if it were a working capability — either the vitals mention is removed, or it is annotated the same way `journey-mode.md`/`page-mode.md`/`browser-review.md` already annotate their own vitals gaps (an in-place gap note, not a silent capability claim).
- A grep for `batch` and `snapshot -i -c` across `plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md` after the change returns no hits describing them as current, working syntax.
- The migrated section still cross-references `journey-mode.md`'s worked example (or inlines an equivalent one) so a reader isn't left to reconstruct the sequential-command pattern from scratch.

## Technical Approach
Read `journey-mode.md`'s "Assemble the sequence" section (lines ~19-33) as the template — it already solved this exact translation for a sibling mode (journey walking) and its solution (sequential commands, vitals gap noted in place) is the established convention this record should reuse verbatim, not reinvent. Apply the same transformation to `discover-mode.md`'s Phase 3 walk description and its four numbered steps.

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md` — replace the `batch` invocation description (~line 111) and update the numbered walk steps (~lines 113-118) that reference "the batched output" and "vitals"

## Gotchas
- `discover-mode.md`'s walk steps also reference "annotated screenshot" (the overlay-numbering convention) — that is a separate, already-filed gap (#2671, "redesign element-reference convention") with its own open design decision. This record's scope is narrowly the `batch`/`vitals` syntax migration; do not also redesign the overlay/element-reference convention here — leave those mentions as-is (or apply #2671's resolution if it has already landed by the time this record is worked) to avoid two records racing to edit the same lines with different conventions.
- Confirm `journey-mode.md`'s worked example is still current (not itself stale) before copying its pattern — re-read it fresh rather than trusting this record's summary of it.

## Original request

visual-review/discover-mode.md: migrate stale batch/snapshot/vitals syntax to Playwright CLI

**Related:** #2647, #2646

Context: `plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md` (line ~111) still describes a `batch` invocation bundling `open`/`snapshot -i -c`/annotated `screenshot`/`vitals` — now-broken under Playwright CLI. Excluded from the 5-part migration (#2645-#2649) since it carries no literal "agent-browser" string, but that check missed non-prefixed old-syntax command references.

Scope: Migrate the one `batch` invocation to Playwright CLI syntax, reusing #2646/#2647's already-resolved gaps (batch and vitals both confirmed no-equivalent — sequential commands + omitted vitals note).

groups.title: visual-review: redesign element-reference convention and Web Vitals replacement post-Playwright-CLI migration
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
The playwright-cli-consumer-migration (#2645-#2649) removed two `agent-browser` capabilities that `visual-review/*` skill files depended on, with no replacement designed:

1. **Screenshot overlay-numbering** — `playwright-cli screenshot` has no `--annotate`-style flag (confirmed during #2645's migration; `playwright-cli-reference.md`'s Screenshot row), so captured screenshots carry no bounding-box/numbered-marker overlay. `plugin/skills/visual-review/browser-review.md` (line ~29) already flags this in place: "Every instruction below that says 'reference overlay numbers' describes the pre-migration convention; until a replacement element-referencing convention is designed, reference elements by clear description ... or by the `eN` ref from the most recent `snapshot` instead." At least 18 prose mentions of "overlay number"/"annotated screenshot"/"annotated overlay" remain across six files (`SKILL.md`, `browser-review.md`, `discover-mode.md`, `journey-mode.md`, `page-mode.md`, `qa-accelerated.md`), each still describing the old overlay-number convention rather than the interim `eN`-ref fallback.
2. **Web Vitals capture** — Playwright CLI has no `vitals` command or equivalent; no built-in surface captures LCP/CLS/INP/TTFB/FCP (confirmed against the CLI's own published docs during #2647's migration; `playwright-cli-reference.md`'s Operation vocabulary table). `browser-review.md` (line ~136) already flags this: Performance findings sourced from vitals cannot currently be produced; the instruction today is to omit the Performance line from the Step 6 report header rather than fabricate values. A hand-written `eval` script against `PerformanceObserver`/the `web-vitals` library is named as a *possible* manual workaround but explicitly not prescribed.

Both gaps were flagged in place by #2647 (in-line HTML comments and prose notes marking "no equivalent found" / "capability gap") but neither was redesigned — the flags are acknowledgments, not solutions.

## Deliverables
1. Decide and document one element-reference convention to replace overlay numbers across every affected file: either (a) standardize on referencing elements by the `eN` ref from the most recent `snapshot` (already suggested as an interim fallback in `browser-review.md` line ~29), or (b) a different convention if `eN` refs prove insufficient for this skill's reporting needs (e.g. they're ephemeral and regenerate per snapshot, which may not survive into a written report the way a numbered overlay did).
2. Update every prose mention across `visual-review/SKILL.md`, `browser-review.md`, `discover-mode.md`, `journey-mode.md`, `page-mode.md`, and `qa-accelerated.md` (the ~18+ occurrences found) from "reference overlay numbers" / "annotated overlay [N]" language to the chosen replacement convention.
3. Decide whether to prescribe an `eval`/`PerformanceObserver` (or `web-vitals` library) vitals workaround as a documented, supported capture mechanism, or to formally accept that Performance findings are unavailable until Playwright CLI ships a vitals equivalent.
4. If prescribing a vitals workaround: document the exact `eval` script/invocation pattern in `playwright-cli-reference.md` and/or `browser-review.md`'s "Vitals interpretation" section, replacing the current "omit the Performance line" instruction with the new capture step.
5. If accepting unavailability: remove or rewrite the "omit the Performance line" language to read as a settled decision rather than an open gap, and note the decision's rationale (e.g. no reliable workaround, or the workaround's fidelity/complexity cost wasn't worth it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- No remaining prose in `visual-review/*.md` describes "annotated overlay [N]" or "reference overlay numbers" as the current, working convention — every such mention either uses the new convention or is clearly marked as describing pre-migration behavior for historical/comparison purposes only.
- `browser-review.md`'s "Overlay-numbering gap" note (line ~29) and its "Capability gap" vitals note (line ~136) are replaced with settled guidance (not open gap descriptions) reflecting whichever decision was made for each of the two capabilities.
- If a vitals workaround was chosen: a documented invocation exists (e.g. in `playwright-cli-reference.md` or `browser-review.md`) that a builder can copy-paste to capture at least one of LCP/CLS/INP/TTFB/FCP via `eval`.
- If vitals unavailability was accepted: the report structure (Step 6 findings table, per `browser-review.md`) no longer references an "omit Performance line" caveat as pending — it reflects the settled absence of a Performance finding category.
- A grep for `overlay \[` or `annotated overlay` across `plugin/skills/visual-review/*.md` after the change returns zero unresolved (pre-decision) hits.

## Technical Approach
Read `plugin/skills/visual-review/browser-review.md`'s two capability-gap notes (line ~29 for overlay-numbering, line ~136 for vitals) as the canonical starting point — both already state the constraint and a candidate direction. For overlay-numbering, evaluate whether `eN` refs (session-scoped, regenerate on every snapshot per `playwright-cli-reference.md`'s Cautions section) are stable enough to reference in a written report that a human reads after the session ends; if not, design an alternative (e.g. a manually-maintained numbered list derived from the snapshot text at report-write time). For vitals, evaluate the `eval`/`PerformanceObserver` workaround's practicality (browser support, whether Playwright CLI's `eval` command can run an async `PerformanceObserver` callback and return timing data) before committing to prescribing it.

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/browser-review.md` — replace the "Overlay-numbering gap" note (~line 29) and "Capability gap (Playwright CLI migration)" vitals note (~line 136) with settled guidance; update the Shared review contract's "Vitals interpretation (Step 1)" section per the vitals decision
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/SKILL.md` — update the Anti-Patterns table's overlay/vitals rows (~lines 224-225) to reflect the new convention
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md` — update overlay/annotated-screenshot/vitals references (~lines 111, 115, 118)
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/journey-mode.md` — update overlay/vitals references and the existing vitals-gap comment (~lines 19-22, 49-53)
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md` — update overlay/vitals references and the existing vitals-gap comment (~lines 19-20, 118, 134, 157, 189, 230, 241, 249)
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/qa-accelerated.md` — update overlay/vitals references (~lines 15, 32, 49)
- `plugin/skills/browse/playwright-cli-reference.md` — if a vitals `eval` workaround is prescribed, document the exact command pattern here alongside the existing negative-result row for "Capture Web Vitals"

## Gotchas
- `eN` refs are explicitly documented as ephemeral (regenerate on every snapshot, per `playwright-cli-reference.md`'s Cautions) — a report written after the session ends may reference a ref that no longer resolves to anything if a new snapshot was taken later in the same session. Any `eN`-based convention needs a rule for when a ref is "frozen" for reporting purposes (e.g. capture ref + description together at the moment of finding, not after the fact).
- The vitals decision is genuinely open in this record — do not treat prescribing the `eval` workaround as the obviously-correct choice without evaluating whether it's reliable and maintainable; accepting unavailability is an equally valid outcome if the workaround proves fragile.
- This record's scope spans six files with a large mention count; verify the full mention list with a fresh grep before considering the sweep complete, since new mentions may have been added to these files since this record was filed.

## Original request

visual-review: redesign element-reference convention and Web Vitals replacement post-Playwright-CLI migration

**Related:** #2647

Context: The playwright-cli-consumer-migration (#2645-#2649) removed two visual-review capabilities with no replacement: screenshot overlay-numbering (no --annotate equivalent) and Web Vitals capture (no LCP/CLS/INP/TTFB command). Both flagged in place by #2647, neither redesigned.

Scope: Redesign the element-reference convention for a no-overlay world (~25+ prose mentions across visual-review/*), and decide whether to prescribe an eval/PerformanceObserver vitals workaround or accept Performance findings as unavailable.

groups.title: Add a UI/UX heuristics review lens
groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2628

## Current State
A social-media Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed) lists roughly 20 UI/UX heuristics — reduce choices per screen, use large targets, favor familiar patterns, group related info, chunk content, keep interactions under 400ms, highlight the primary action, keep key actions nearby, put essentials first, end flows memorably, show visible progress, simplify complex interfaces, use sensible defaults, prevent errors proactively, make errors recoverable, keep patterns consistent, visually connect related elements, reduce task time, reveal complexity gradually, and make completion feel close. No existing claude-tweaks skill applies a UX-heuristics lens during review or build — the closest existing checks (#2622, #2624, #2625, #2628) are backend/security-focused and don't touch interaction-design quality.

## Deliverables
1. A reusable UI/UX heuristics checklist (the ~20 items above, normalized into policy-row form: heuristic name, what it flags, and an example violation) stored where a review-stage skill can load it — either as a new section of an existing review skill (`/claude-tweaks:review` or `/claude-tweaks:visual-review`) or a new lightweight lens file under that skill's directory.
2. Wiring so a build/review pass can run the checklist against a rendered screen or component and flag violations — e.g., "no visible progress on a long-running operation," "primary action not visually highlighted," "more than N top-level choices on one screen."
3. A short usage note (in the hosting skill's own docs) describing when the lens applies (Surface: web/mobile/desktop records) versus when it doesn't (backend/infra work with no rendered UI).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The checklist exists as a standalone, reusable artifact (a markdown lens file or skill section) — not merely restated in this issue's text.
- The checklist enumerates each of the ~20 heuristics as a distinct, checkable row (heuristic + what a violation looks like), not a single paragraph.
- Running the checklist against at least one sample screen or component that violates a known heuristic (e.g., a long-running action with no progress indicator) produces a flagged finding naming that specific heuristic.
- Running the checklist against a sample screen with no violations produces no false-positive flags for the heuristics it does check.
- The lens is invocable from at least one existing review-stage skill's normal flow (`/claude-tweaks:review` and/or `/claude-tweaks:visual-review`), not only as a standalone document nobody calls.

## Technical Approach
Normalize the ~20 heuristics from the source Reel into a policy-row table (name | signal to look for | example violation), mirroring the existing policy-row conventions already used elsewhere in this repo's review-stage skills. Host the table as a new lens file cited by whichever existing review skill already inspects rendered UI, rather than duplicating review-orchestration logic. Gate invocation on `Surface: web/mobile/desktop` records (per the repo's existing frontend-detection signal) so backend/infra records never pay for a UX pass that doesn't apply to them.

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/SKILL.md` — candidate host for the new UX-heuristics lens invocation during a visual review pass.
- `plugin/skills/review/SKILL.md` — alternate/additional candidate host if the lens should also run during code review of UI-affecting changes.
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md` — existing Surface-detection signal to gate when the lens applies.
- A new lens file, path determined by whichever host skill is chosen (e.g. `plugin/skills/visual-review/ux-heuristics-lens.md`) — holds the normalized ~20-item checklist.

## Gotchas
- The heuristics originate from a single unsourced social-media Reel, not a cited UX research source — treat each item as a heuristic prompt to check for, not a hard rule to enforce mechanically; some (e.g. "sub-400ms interactions") may not be measurable without instrumentation this repo doesn't have, and should be phrased as a manual-inspection prompt rather than an automated metric check.
- Overlap risk with Impeccable's existing design-critique surface (`impeccable:impeccable-finish-reviewer`) — confirm this lens complements rather than duplicates checks Impeccable already performs before finalizing which skill hosts it.
- Keep the checklist's scope to UI/UX heuristics only; do not fold in the existing backend/security checks (#2622, #2624, #2625, #2628) it's meant to sit alongside.

## Original request

Add a UI/UX heuristics review lens

Current State:
- Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed) lists ~20 UI/UX heuristics: reduce choices per screen, large targets, familiar patterns, group related info, chunk content, sub-400ms interactions, highlight primary action, key actions nearby, essentials first, memorable flow endings, visible progress, simplify complex interfaces, sensible defaults, proactive error prevention, recoverable errors, pattern consistency, visually connected related elements, reduced task time, gradual complexity reveal, and "make completion feel closer."
- No existing claude-tweaks skill applies a UX-heuristics lens during review/build — existing checks are backend/security-focused (#2622, #2624, #2625, #2628).

Deliverables:
- Add the list as a policy-row checklist to an existing review skill (or a new lightweight one) so a build/review pass can flag obvious violations (no visible progress on long ops, primary action not highlighted, etc.).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Checklist is available as a reusable lens, not just this issue's text.
- Running it against a sample screen flags at least one applicable item when violated.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcwkX6OyduT/

groups.title: Add pre-launch security hardening checklist for AI-built apps
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

The plugin has no dedicated pre-launch security check for the failure patterns common in AI-generated web apps: secrets embedded in the client bundle instead of server-side env vars, routes returning user data with no per-user ownership check (missing Supabase RLS or equivalent), and AI-model-calling endpoints with no auth, per-user rate limiting, input-length cap, or provider spend alert. `plugin/skills/code-health/SKILL.md` already has an extension point built for exactly this kind of repo-wide, criterion-driven check — `focus=<vertical>` mode (documented in `code-health/SKILL.md`'s "Focus Mode" section): a deterministic generator produces a fixed candidate set repo-wide, and the focus pins its own judging criterion in place of `criteriaForArea`'s area-type lookup, while dedup/fingerprint/file-issue (Steps 2, 5+) run unchanged. `plugin/skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Code-Mode Procedure already has a precedent for a component-skill step invoked mid-pipeline: Step 6.5 (Design Quality Pass via `/claude-tweaks:design-wrapper`) and Step 6 (visual-review recommendation).

A structurally parallel record, #2622 ("Add a pre-scale hardening skill for AI-coded apps"), proposes a new standalone skill (`/scale-readiness`) walking a codebase through a different but adjacent set of checks (query/background-job/caching/pooling/monitoring). #2625 ("Add GDPR account-deletion vs. backup-retention check") is a third, already-shaped, narrower security-adjacent check (cryptographic erasure for backup retention). None of the three currently cross-reference each other's scope boundary in a shared doc.

## Deliverables

1. A security-hardening check covering exactly the three named categories: (a) no secrets in the client bundle (server-side env vars only), (b) per-user ownership checks / RLS-equivalent enforcement on every table/route returning user data, (c) auth + per-user rate limiting + input-length cap + provider spend alert on every AI-model-calling endpoint.
2. One copy-paste prompt per check (three total), matching the prompt-pattern convention already used elsewhere in the pipeline (e.g. the verbatim-command style prompts in existing skill sub-files) — each prompt runnable standalone by a user without invoking the full skill.
3. Implemented as a new `focus=<vertical>` criterion + candidate generator in `plugin/skills/code-health/`, following the existing Focus Mode extension pattern (`code-health/SKILL.md`'s Focus Mode section, `focus-mode.md`'s registry lookup) rather than a parallel bolt-on mechanism.
4. A new step in `plugin/skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Code-Mode Procedure invoking this check as a component skill (mirroring Step 6.5's Design Quality Pass pattern), so it also runs "as a step within /review."
5. Documentation in the new criterion/generator's own file (or `code-health/SKILL.md`'s Focus Mode section) explicitly stating the scope boundary against #2622 (performance/scale) and #2625 (GDPR/backup retention) — what this check owns vs. what it explicitly does not, so future work doesn't duplicate scope across the three.
6. `docs/skill-graph.md` updated per CLAUDE.md's "Every relationship between skills is stated once" convention, since this adds a new cross-skill edge (code-health focus criterion invoked from review).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `/claude-tweaks:code-health focus=<the-new-vertical-name>` against a sample vibecoded app fixture containing all three violation patterns (a client-bundle secret, a route missing an ownership check, an unthrottled AI-calling endpoint with no spend alert) flags a distinct finding for each of the three categories.
- Running the same check against a fixture with none of the three violations present produces zero findings for this criterion (no false positives on clean code).
- `plugin/skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Code-Mode Procedure invokes the new check as a numbered step, and `/claude-tweaks:review {n}` on a spec-record touching client/server boundary code exercises that step.
- The new criterion's own documentation (or `code-health/SKILL.md`) states, in prose, how its scope differs from #2622's pre-scale hardening and #2625's GDPR/backup-retention check — no overlapping category is claimed by two of the three.
- `docs/skill-graph.md` lists the new edge (the new review step invoking the code-health focus criterion).
- `npm test` passes in full after the change.

## Technical Approach

Add a new focus-mode vertical to `code-health`'s generator registry (per `focus-mode.md`'s registry lookup convention — never hand-listed in `SKILL.md` itself, per that file's own IL-40 note), with a dedicated candidate generator that scans for: (a) client-bundle files (build output or client-side source under a recognized framework's client directory) containing a literal API-key/secret pattern, (b) route/handler files returning user-scoped data with no visible ownership predicate (a `WHERE user_id = `-shaped filter, an RLS policy reference, or equivalent) in the same file or its immediately-composed query, (c) route/handler files calling a recognized AI-model SDK/API with no visible auth middleware, rate-limit decorator/middleware, input-length validation, or spend-alert/budget-check reference nearby. Each candidate is judged by a dedicated criterion (per `criteriaForArea`'s pinning pattern) rather than the generic area-type lookup, following the existing Focus Mode contract exactly (Steps 2 and 5+ unchanged, only scoping/candidate-generation and criterion selection are new).

Wire this focus criterion into `plugin/skills/review/SKILL.md` as a new step in the Code-Mode Procedure, following the Step 6.5 Design Quality Pass precedent: a numbered step that invokes the code-health focus run as a component skill and folds its findings into the review's own summary (Step 7), governed by its own contract per that pattern (Next-Actions omitted when invoked from `/review`, per the Component-Skill Contract convention `review/SKILL.md` already documents for its other component steps).

Write the three copy-paste prompts as literal, standalone text blocks in the new criterion's documentation — one per check category — so a user can run any single check manually without invoking the full skill, matching the pattern the record itself asks for ("matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the pipeline").

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/code-health/focus-mode.md` — register the new vertical in the generator registry, following its documented registry-lookup convention.
- `plugin/skills/code-health/` — new generator module/criterion file (naming follows the directory's existing per-vertical file convention) implementing the three candidate-detection heuristics and their judging criterion.
- `plugin/skills/code-health/SKILL.md` — Focus Mode section: no hand-listing of the new vertical name (per IL-40), but confirm the section's prose still describes the mechanism accurately if anything vertical-count-dependent is stated.
- `plugin/skills/review/SKILL.md` — add the new numbered step to the Code-Mode Procedure (Steps 1-7 list, "## Overview"/"## Review Modes" table rows referencing step numbers), following the Step 6.5 Design Quality Pass precedent for a component-skill invocation.
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — add the new cross-skill edge per CLAUDE.md's single-source-of-truth convention for skill relationships.
- Related-record cross-reference: the new criterion's own doc (or a shared location both this and #2622/#2625 can cite) stating the three checks' scope boundaries.

## Gotchas

- The client-bundle-secret detection heuristic risks false positives on legitimate public keys (a Stripe publishable key, a public API endpoint identifier) that are safe to ship client-side — the criterion must distinguish "looks like a secret pattern" from "is actually a private/server-only credential," or it will flag safe code and train users to ignore the check.
- The per-user-ownership-check heuristic is necessarily approximate — it can only detect the *absence* of a recognizable ownership predicate near the query, not verify that an existing predicate is actually correct (scoped to the right user, not bypassable). This is a "flag for human review" check, not a formal proof.
- Detecting "no rate limiting middleware nearby" for AI-calling endpoints depends on recognizing whatever middleware/decorator convention the target codebase uses — this will vary widely across frameworks (Express middleware, Next.js route handlers, a custom decorator), so the generator's coverage boundary (per IL-110's convention that every generator states its own coverage boundary) must be explicit about which frameworks/patterns it recognizes and which it does not.
- Overlap risk with #2622 and #2625 is real: #2622's pre-scale skill and this check both touch "endpoint hardening" territory (rate limiting appears in both problem statements), and #2625's GDPR check is a narrower security-adjacent concern. The scope-boundary documentation (Deliverable 5) is not optional polish — without it, a future contributor extending any of the three is likely to duplicate a check the others already own.
- This record's own Deliverables text hedges on exact placement ("such as /security-review or /code-health, or a small standalone skill") — `/security-review` in that phrasing refers to the separate, personal top-level skill outside this plugin (not a `claude-tweaks:` skill), so the only in-plugin candidates are `/code-health`'s focus-mode extension point (chosen here) or a wholly new standalone skill; the Focus Mode route was chosen because it reuses an existing, tested mechanism (dedup, fingerprinting, issue-filing) rather than duplicating that machinery in a new skill.

## Original request

Add pre-launch security hardening checklist for AI-built apps

Current State:
- AI-coded apps often ship with API keys or secrets embedded in the client bundle instead of server-side env vars.
- Routes that return user data frequently lack a per-user ownership check (e.g. missing Supabase RLS policies), letting one user read another's records.
- Endpoints that call an AI model often have no auth, per-user rate limiting, input-length cap, or provider spend alert.

Deliverables:
- Add a pre-launch security checklist to claude-tweaks (new policy rows on an existing skill such as /security-review or /code-health, or a small standalone skill) covering: no secrets in the client bundle, per-user ownership checks / RLS on every table, and auth + rate limiting + spend alerts on every AI-calling endpoint.
- Ship one copy-paste prompt per check, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the pipeline.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running the check against a sample vibecoded app flags a violation in each of the three categories when present.
- Docs note how this relates to the existing pre-scale hardening work (issue #2622) so the two don't duplicate scope.
- Works standalone and as a step within /review or /build.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdT9C-fqI9V/

**Related:** #2622, #2625

groups.title: Migrate status-line instruction: browse, simplify, help, visual-review, transcript-judge, feedback
groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

Part of the 5-unit status-line migration decomposition (parent #2264, keystone #2265). This unit
covers the remaining 7 files not covered by WU2, WU3, or WU4 — browse, simplify, help,
visual-review (2 files), `_shared/transcript-judge.md`, and feedback — each a pure mechanical text
replacement of the old first-line-position instruction.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 3 (grouped as: task 1 — the 4 pure wording-only files (`simplify/SKILL.md`,
`help/status-scan.md`, `_shared/transcript-judge.md`, plus confirming `feedback/session-evaluation.md`'s
template reorder); task 2 — the 3 Template A ordering-reversal files (`browse/SKILL.md`,
`visual-review/page-mode.md`, `visual-review/discover-mode.md`); task 3 — verification (`npm
test` plus the greps in Acceptance Criteria below))

## Non-Goals

- Editing the canonical contract file itself, or `subagent-stop.js`'s detection logic — that is
  #2265, which this unit is `Blocked by`.
- Editing any file outside the 7 listed below — those belong to WU2, WU3, or WU4 in this same
  decomposition.
- Changing the four status words themselves or the Template A/B/C content that follows the status
  line.

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/browse/SKILL.md` (~116-118): `Each agent's first reply line must still be one of
  \`DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED\`, then the chosen template.`
- `plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md` (~75): `First reply line MUST be one of: DONE /
  DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED.`
- `plugin/skills/help/status-scan.md` (~11): `status line first (\`DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS /
  NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED\`)`
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md` (~59): `Each agent's first reply line must be one of
  \`DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED\`, then the table.`
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md` (~109): `Each agent's first reply line must be
  one of \`DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED\`, then the table.`
- `plugin/skills/_shared/transcript-judge.md` (~152-153): `The status line is the contract's usual
  DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED first line, per
  \`_shared/subagent-output-contract.md\`.`
- `plugin/skills/feedback/session-evaluation.md` (~20-22): output template's first line is the
  bare enum, positioned first in the inlined template block.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `plugin/skills/browse/SKILL.md` (~116-118) — replace with: `Each agent's reply must end with
      its last non-empty line reading exactly \`STATUS: DONE\` (or DONE_WITH_CONCERNS /
      NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED), then the chosen template.` — reversing today's "status line, then
      template" order to "template, then trailing status line."
- [ ] `plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md` (~75) — replace with: `The reply's last non-empty line
      MUST read exactly \`STATUS: DONE\` (or DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED).`
- [ ] `plugin/skills/help/status-scan.md` (~11) — replace with: `trailing status line
      (\`STATUS: DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED\`)`
- [ ] `plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md` (~59) — replace with: `Each agent's reply must end
      with its last non-empty line reading exactly \`STATUS: DONE\` (or DONE_WITH_CONCERNS /
      NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED), then the table.` — reversing today's "status line, then table"
      order.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md` (~109) — same replacement text as the
      `page-mode.md` deliverable above (identical shape, separate file).
- [ ] `plugin/skills/_shared/transcript-judge.md` (~152-153) — replace with: `The status line is
      the contract's usual DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / NEEDS_CONTEXT / BLOCKED trailing
      \`STATUS: {WORD}\` line (the last non-empty line of the reply), per
      \`_shared/subagent-output-contract.md\`.`
- [ ] `plugin/skills/feedback/session-evaluation.md` (~20-22) — move the bare enum out of the
      first-position slot in the inlined output template and reposition it as the template's final
      line, labeled `STATUS: {WORD}` — `{WORD}` here is a literal template placeholder (matching
      this same file's own existing placeholder convention for the rest of its inlined template),
      not literal text to render as-is; the actually-emitted line is one of `STATUS: DONE` /
      `STATUS: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` / `STATUS: NEEDS_CONTEXT` / `STATUS: BLOCKED`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All 7 files read the new trailing-`STATUS:`-line instruction; none still asserts "first
   line"/"first reply line"/"status line first" as the required position.
2. `browse/SKILL.md`, `visual-review/page-mode.md`, and `visual-review/discover-mode.md` each
   reflect the reversed order for their Template A-shaped dispatch (chosen template/table first,
   trailing status line last) rather than merely relabeling the old "status line, then
   template/table" order.
3. `feedback/session-evaluation.md`'s inlined output template has the status enum repositioned to
   the template's last line, not its first — this is a structural template reorder, not a wording
   swap only.
4. `grep -rln "first reply line\|first line\|status line first" plugin/skills/browse/SKILL.md
   plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md plugin/skills/help/status-scan.md
   plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md
   plugin/skills/_shared/transcript-judge.md plugin/skills/feedback/session-evaluation.md` returns
   no match against any of the edited status-line instructions.
5. Structural checks for the 3 reordered files, matching AC4's rigor: for each of
   `browse/SKILL.md`, `visual-review/page-mode.md`, and `visual-review/discover-mode.md`, the
   line containing `STATUS:` in the edited instruction appears textually after the line
   describing the template/table it follows (a simple line-number comparison via `grep -n`
   against both phrases in the same file) — proving the reorder actually happened, not just that
   old wording is gone. For `feedback/session-evaluation.md`, the `STATUS:` placeholder line is
   the last line of the inlined output-template code block, confirmed by inspecting the block's
   closing fence position relative to it.
6. No test outside this unit's 7 files pins the retired wording being replaced here — confirmed
   by `grep -rln "first reply line\|first line\|status line first"
   plugin/skills/browse/SKILL.md plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md plugin/skills/help/status-scan.md
   plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md
   plugin/skills/_shared/transcript-judge.md plugin/skills/feedback/session-evaluation.md tests/`
   run once against the union of this unit's files plus `tests/` (rather than the files alone),
   before this unit's own edits land, returning matches only inside the 7 files above (never
   inside `tests/`); if a test file does match, that's a pre-existing conformance test pinning
   this exact prose — surface it as a blocker rather than editing the source file out from under
   it, since a byte-pinned test failing is this repo's own signal to update the test in the same
   commit, not a signal to skip the source edit.
7. `npm test` passes with no regressions.

## Technical Approach

Mechanical text replacement for 4 of the 7 files (`simplify/SKILL.md`, `help/status-scan.md`,
`_shared/transcript-judge.md`, plus wording updates), matching the canonical trailing-line phrasing
#2265 establishes. Three files additionally need structural reordering, not just a wording swap:
`browse/SKILL.md`, `visual-review/page-mode.md`, and `visual-review/discover-mode.md` are all
Template A-shaped dispatch sites (status line then table/template, today), so each moves its
status-line instruction to describe a trailing position after the table/template instead; and
`feedback/session-evaluation.md`'s inlined output template literally has the enum positioned first
in the template block, so that block's own line order changes, not merely the prose describing it.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/browse/SKILL.md` — lines ~116-118; also needs Template A ordering reversed.
- `plugin/skills/simplify/SKILL.md` — line ~75, wording only.
- `plugin/skills/help/status-scan.md` — line ~11, wording only.
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/page-mode.md` — line ~59; also needs Template A ordering reversed.
- `plugin/skills/visual-review/discover-mode.md` — line ~109; also needs Template A ordering
  reversed.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/transcript-judge.md` — lines ~152-153, wording only (this file reads a
  status line rather than dispatching one, but its own description of where to find it must match
  the new convention).
- `plugin/skills/feedback/session-evaluation.md` — lines ~20-22; the inlined output template's
  line order changes, not just wording.

## Gotchas

- Three files in this batch (`browse/SKILL.md`, `visual-review/page-mode.md`,
  `visual-review/discover-mode.md`) need their stated status-line/table ordering reversed, not
  just re-worded — the same reversal WU4's `tidy/scan-execution.md` deliverable needs, since all
  four are Template A dispatch sites.
- `feedback/session-evaluation.md`'s change is structural (move a template line), not textual —
  read the actual inlined template block before editing, don't just search-and-replace the enum
  string in place.
- `_shared/transcript-judge.md` is a consumer of the status line (it reads a prior agent's already
  -emitted status to judge a transcript), not a dispatcher of one — its edit only needs to
  describe the new location correctly, it issues no dispatch instruction of its own.
- This unit is `Blocked by` #2265 — the exact replacement wording must match the canonical text
  #2265 lands, not a guess at what it will say. The strings quoted in Deliverables above are this
  record's best-effort snapshot at authoring time; re-read #2265's actual landed text in
  `subagent-output-contract.md` before applying any edit here and defer to it if the two differ.

## Manual Steps

None — every deliverable is a direct file edit plus `npm test`.

groups.title: Add secrets-manager + rotation check to the security checklist
groups.body:
Surface: backend

**Related:** #2665

## Current State
A social-media Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed) gives a three-step fix for long-lived hard-coded API keys: (1) move secrets to a dedicated secrets manager (Doppler, Infisical, or AWS Secrets Manager are named as examples) that fetches at runtime instead of bundling secrets at deploy time — not a `.env` file or the hosting platform's dashboard; (2) dual-key rotation — generate the new key, deploy it, verify traffic against it, then revoke the old one, so two keys remain valid during the transition window (zero downtime); (3) automate the rotation schedule (e.g. a cron job every 30 days) so a leaked key's blast radius is capped at the rotation interval instead of being unbounded. This extends the pre-launch security checklist (`#2624`), which currently covers "no secrets in client bundle" but not secret-storage or rotation strategy — a related but distinct concern (a secret can be correctly kept server-side and still be a long-lived, unrotatable, single point of compromise). `#2624` is currently unbuilt (open, no shipped skill implementation).

## Deliverables
1. A checklist row verifying secrets live in a dedicated secrets manager fetched at runtime, rather than a `.env` file committed or deployed alongside the app, or values entered only into the hosting platform's dashboard with no independent management layer.
2. A checklist row verifying a documented key-rotation procedure exists, specifically one that supports dual-key validity during a transition window (new key generated and deployed, traffic verified, then the old key revoked) rather than a rotation that requires downtime or breaks in-flight requests.
3. A checklist row verifying the rotation schedule is automated (e.g., a scheduled job) rather than manual-only or undocumented, so a leaked key's exposure window is bounded by the rotation interval instead of being open-ended.
4. Documentation cross-referencing `#2624`, explicitly distinguishing this record's scope (where secrets live and how they're rotated) from `#2624`'s "no secrets in client bundle" check (whether a secret leaks into client-visible code at all) — the two are complementary, not overlapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The secrets-manager check, run against a sample app whose secrets are read only from a `.env` file with no dedicated secrets-manager integration, flags a violation.
- The secrets-manager check, run against a sample app that fetches secrets at runtime from a dedicated manager (any of Doppler, Infisical, AWS Secrets Manager, or an equivalent), passes without a false-positive flag.
- The rotation-procedure check flags an app with no documented rotation procedure at all, and passes an app whose documented procedure supports dual-key validity during a transition window.
- The rotation-schedule check flags a rotation procedure that is manual-only (no automation, no defined interval), and passes one wired to a scheduled job with a defined interval.
- Documentation cross-references `#2624` by number and states explicitly how this record's scope differs from `#2624`'s existing "no secrets in client bundle" row.

## Technical Approach
Since `#2624` has no shipped skill implementation yet, land this as a standalone secrets-lifecycle checklist section (same pattern already established for `#2657`, `#2663`, and `#2665`'s own additions to the same unbuilt `#2624`), written to merge cleanly into `#2624`'s eventual body/skill once that record ships. None of the three checklist rows are name-specific to a particular secrets-manager vendor — the check verifies the *properties* (runtime fetch vs. deploy-time bundling; dual-key rotation support; automated schedule), detectable via looking for the absence of raw secret values in deploy-time config/build artifacts and the presence of a secrets-manager SDK/client library import, rather than hardcoding a check for any one named vendor's API.

### Key Files
- A new checklist file (path determined by whichever skill or doc structure `#2624`'s implementation adopts, e.g. under `plugin/skills/` if a security-checklist skill is created, or `docs/reference/` if it remains a static checklist) — holds the three secrets-lifecycle rows and their audit prompts.
- `#2624`'s own body/eventual implementation file — cross-reference added once both records have landed, with an explicit scope-boundary note distinguishing this record's rows from `#2624`'s existing client-bundle-secrets row.

## Gotchas
- `#2624` is unbuilt as of this shaping — there is no live checklist artifact to append rows to today; this record may ship first as a standalone section, and whichever record ships second must fold the others in with cross-references, avoiding silently-diverging checklists (same build-order caveat already noted on `#2657`, `#2663`, `#2665`).
- Detecting "secrets fetched at runtime from a dedicated manager" via static inspection is inherently approximate — an app could import a secrets-manager SDK but still hardcode a fallback secret elsewhere, or could correctly avoid `.env` files while using a home-grown runtime-fetch mechanism this check wouldn't recognize as a "dedicated manager." Frame findings as "likely mismatch, flag for human review" rather than a definitive pass/fail, consistent with how `#2663`'s privacy-policy-accuracy check is already framed.
- Do not conflate this record's rotation-procedure/schedule checks with `#2624`'s client-bundle-secrets check — a secret can pass `#2624`'s row (never appears in client code) while still failing every row this record adds (no manager, no rotation, no schedule); keep the two checklist rows sets and their pass/fail logic independent.

## Original request

Add secrets-manager + rotation check to the security checklist

Current State:
- Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed) gives a three-step fix for long-lived hard-coded API keys: (1) move secrets to a dedicated manager (Doppler, Infisical, or AWS Secrets Manager) that fetches at runtime instead of bundling at deploy time — not a .env file or the host's dashboard; (2) dual-key rotation — generate the new key, deploy it, verify traffic, then revoke the old one, so two keys are valid during the transition window (zero downtime); (3) automate the rotation schedule (e.g. a cron job every 30 days) so a leak's blast radius is capped at the rotation interval instead of being unbounded.
- Extends the pre-launch security checklist (#2624), which covers "no secrets in client bundle" but not secret storage/rotation strategy.

Deliverables:
- Add a secrets-lifecycle check to #2624: are secrets in a dedicated manager (not .env/dashboard), is there a rotation procedure, and is it scheduled/automated rather than manual-only.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Check flags apps using only .env/host-dashboard secrets with no manager or rotation schedule.
- Docs cross-reference #2624.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZGYLpLPDR-/

groups.title: Add Cloudflare WAF/rate-limiting config check for auth endpoints
groups.body:
Surface: backend

**Related:** #2663

## Current State
A social-media Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed) states a concrete claim: an unconfigured Cloudflare setup still passes credential-stuffing traffic, scrapers, and vulnerability scanners straight through to the origin even though Cloudflare sits in front of it — because rate limiting on auth endpoints, bot management on high-value pages, and custom WAF rules for known attack patterns are opt-in, not default. Cloudflare being "in front of" an app is not itself a security control; the actual hardening comes from the specific rules configured within it. This is directly relevant to this environment: Cloudflare Tunnel already runs for the homelab (per `claude-user-config:cloudflare`), and the same opt-in-not-default gap applies to any app-level Cloudflare zone in front of an AI-built app. This extends the pre-launch security checklist (`#2624`), which is currently unbuilt (open, no shipped skill implementation).

## Deliverables
1. A Cloudflare-hardening checklist row verifying rate limiting is configured specifically on auth-path routes (login, signup, password-reset) — not merely a blanket zone-level rate limit that doesn't distinguish auth endpoints from the rest of the app.
2. A checklist row verifying bot management (or, at minimum, Bot Fight Mode) is enabled on high-value pages — checkout, account creation, any endpoint attractive to credential-stuffing or scraping traffic.
3. A checklist row verifying custom WAF rules exist for known attack signatures relevant to the app's stack, rather than relying solely on Cloudflare's default managed rules.
4. A verification mechanism for each row: where the Cloudflare API can confirm a rule's existence and scope (e.g., listing rate-limiting rules and checking their match expression targets auth paths specifically), prefer an API-based check; where that isn't practical, a manual-review prompt naming exactly what to look for in the Cloudflare dashboard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The rate-limiting check, run against a sample Cloudflare zone configuration with a rate-limiting rule scoped only at the zone level (no path-specific match), flags that auth endpoints aren't specifically covered.
- The rate-limiting check, run against a sample configuration with a rate-limiting rule whose match expression targets `/login`, `/signup`, and `/password-reset` (or equivalent), passes without a false-positive flag.
- The bot-management check flags a zone with Bot Fight Mode (or full bot management) disabled, and passes a zone with it enabled.
- The WAF check flags a zone relying only on Cloudflare's default managed ruleset with no custom rules, and passes a zone with at least one custom rule targeting a named attack pattern.
- Documentation cross-references `#2624` by number, noting the build-order dependency (whichever of the two records ships first stands alone; the other folds it in) the same way `#2657`/`#2663` already establish for their own additions to the same still-unbuilt checklist.

## Technical Approach
Since `#2624` has no shipped skill implementation yet, land this as a standalone Cloudflare-hardening checklist section (same pattern as `#2657`'s JWT checks and `#2663`'s legal/compliance items against the same unbuilt `#2624`), written to merge cleanly into `#2624`'s eventual body/skill once that record ships. Where a check can be automated, use the Cloudflare API (rate limiting rules, bot management settings, and WAF custom rules are all queryable via Cloudflare's REST API) to inspect a zone's actual configuration rather than trusting a self-report that "Cloudflare is enabled." Where API access isn't available or configured for this check to run against, fall back to a manual-review prompt naming the specific dashboard setting to inspect (mirroring `#2663`'s automatable-vs-manual-reminder split for its own checklist rows).

### Key Files
- A new checklist file (path determined by whichever skill or doc structure `#2624`'s implementation adopts, e.g. under `plugin/skills/` if a security-checklist skill is created, or `docs/reference/` if it remains a static checklist) — holds the three Cloudflare-hardening rows and their audit prompts/API-check logic.
- `#2624`'s own body/eventual implementation file — cross-reference added once both records have landed.

## Gotchas
- `#2624` is unbuilt as of this shaping — there is no live checklist artifact to append rows to today; this record may ship first as a standalone section, and whichever record ships second must fold the other in with a cross-reference, avoiding silently-diverging checklists (same build-order caveat as `#2657`/`#2663`).
- An API-based check requires a Cloudflare API token with read access to the relevant zone's rate-limiting, bot-management, and WAF settings — the check's documentation should state this prerequisite explicitly rather than silently failing or reporting a false pass when no token is configured.
- "Rate limiting configured on auth endpoints" is a judgment call about what counts as an auth-path match expression (exact-path match vs. a broader pattern that happens to include auth paths) — the check should flag an ambiguous or overly broad match expression for human review rather than confidently passing or failing it.
- Distinguish this checklist item from a general "is Cloudflare enabled" check — the entire point of this record (per the source claim) is that zone-level presence doesn't imply endpoint-specific hardening; the checklist rows and their pass/fail logic must reflect that distinction, not collapse back into a blanket check.

## Original request

Add Cloudflare WAF/rate-limiting config check for auth endpoints

Current State:
- Reel states a concrete claim: an unconfigured Cloudflare setup still passes credential-stuffing traffic, scrapers, and vulnerability scanners straight through to the origin even though Cloudflare sits in front — because rate limiting on auth endpoints, bot management on high-value pages, and custom WAF rules for known attack patterns are opt-in, not default.
- Directly relevant: the reader already runs Cloudflare Tunnel for the homelab, and this same gap applies to any app-level Cloudflare zone in front of an AI-built app — extends the pre-launch security checklist (#2624).

Deliverables:
- Add a Cloudflare-hardening check to the security checklist (#2624): rate limiting configured on login/signup/password-reset endpoints, bot management (or at least Bot Fight Mode) enabled on high-value pages, and custom WAF rules for known attack signatures — not just "Cloudflare is in front of it."

Acceptance Criteria:
- Check verifies (via API or manual review prompt) that rate-limiting rules exist on auth-path routes specifically, not just a blanket zone-level setting.
- Docs cross-reference #2624.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcRgRM2jjuv/

groups.title: Add legal/compliance pre-launch questions to the security checklist
groups.body:
Surface: backend

**Related:** #2657

## Current State
A social-media Reel (caption states the claim directly; no transcription needed) names three pre-launch questions builders should answer before shipping: (1) do you have cyber liability insurance, (2) have you read your platform's terms of service, and (3) does your privacy policy actually match what your app does. This is adjacent to two existing open records: the pre-launch security hardening checklist (`#2624`, secrets in client bundle, RLS/ownership checks, AI-endpoint auth/rate-limiting) and the GDPR account-deletion vs. backup-retention check (`#2625`) — the "privacy policy matches the app" question specifically overlaps with `#2625`'s data-handling scope, since both are ultimately about whether stated data practices match actual ones. Neither `#2624` nor `#2625` has a shipped checklist/skill implementation yet.

## Deliverables
1. A privacy-policy-accuracy checklist row: an automatable comparison between claims made in a privacy policy document (data collected, third-party services/processors named, retention practices stated) and the app's actual data flows (API calls to third-party services, data fields collected in forms/schemas, retention logic in the codebase) — flagging a mismatch (e.g., an analytics or ad SDK integrated in code but not named in the policy).
2. A terms-of-service pre-launch reminder line: explicitly documented as a manual reminder to read the hosting/platform's ToS before launch, not an automated check — no attempt to parse or verify ToS compliance programmatically, since that's not something a code check can reliably assess.
3. A cyber-liability-insurance pre-launch reminder line: same manual-reminder treatment as the ToS item — a business/financial decision outside any code check's scope.
4. Documentation cross-referencing both `#2624` (the general pre-launch security checklist this item is meant to join) and `#2625` (the GDPR/data-retention check this item's privacy-policy-accuracy row overlaps with), so the checklist and the more specific GDPR check don't silently diverge on what "policy matches practice" means.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The privacy-policy-accuracy check is implemented as an automatable row: given a sample privacy policy document and a sample codebase using at least one third-party service (e.g., an analytics SDK) not mentioned in that policy, the check flags the mismatch.
- The privacy-policy-accuracy check produces no false-positive flag when run against a sample app whose privacy policy correctly names every third-party service actually integrated.
- The ToS and cyber-liability-insurance items appear in the checklist as clearly labeled manual-reminder lines (not run as automated checks), with prose explicitly stating why they aren't automatable.
- The checklist documentation cross-references `#2624` and `#2625` by number, explaining the overlap between this item's privacy-policy-accuracy row and `#2625`'s GDPR scope so a future reader/builder of either doesn't duplicate the other.

## Technical Approach
Since `#2624` has no shipped skill implementation yet, land this as a standalone checklist section (mirroring the approach taken for `#2657`'s JWT checks against the same still-unbuilt `#2624`), written so it merges cleanly into `#2624`'s eventual body/skill once that record ships. The automatable privacy-policy-accuracy check needs two inputs: the privacy policy's stated third-party services/data practices (parsed from the policy document, likely via a simple keyword/entity extraction rather than full NLP) and the codebase's actual third-party integrations (grep for known SDK/API-client imports and outbound API call patterns) — compare the two lists and flag services present in code but absent from the policy. The ToS and insurance items need no implementation beyond a documented reminder line; do not build a mechanism to verify either, since neither is code-inspectable.

### Key Files
- A new checklist file (path determined by whichever skill or doc structure `#2624`'s implementation adopts, e.g. under `plugin/skills/` if a security-checklist skill is created, or `docs/reference/` if it remains a static checklist) — holds the three legal/compliance items and the privacy-policy-accuracy audit prompt.
- `#2624`'s own body/eventual implementation file — cross-reference added once both records have landed.
- `#2625`'s own body — cross-reference added noting the privacy-policy-accuracy row's overlap with GDPR account-deletion/backup-retention scope.

## Gotchas
- `#2624` and `#2625` are both unbuilt as of this shaping — there is no live checklist artifact to append rows to today; this record may ship first as a standalone section, and whichever record ships second must fold the others in with cross-references, avoiding silently-diverging checklists (same build-order caveat as `#2657`).
- The privacy-policy-accuracy check's automation is inherently approximate — keyword/entity matching between a policy document and codebase imports will miss paraphrased policy language or indirect data flows (e.g., a third-party service called via a proxy/wrapper with a generic name); the check should be framed as "flags likely mismatches for human review," not a guarantee of policy accuracy.
- Do not attempt to automate the ToS or insurance items even partially — the record's own framing (from Instagram Reel caption, direct claim, not transcribed) is explicit that these are non-code-inspectable business decisions, and a false-positive-prone automated version of either would undermine trust in the rest of the checklist.

## Original request

Add legal/compliance pre-launch questions to the security checklist

Current State:
- Reel states three pre-launch questions builders should answer: do you have cyber liability insurance, have you read your platform's terms of service, and does your privacy policy actually match what your app does.
- Caption states the full claim directly (not a hook) — no transcription needed.
- Adjacent to the pre-launch security checklist (#2624) and the GDPR/backup-retention issue (#2625): the "privacy policy matches the app" question in particular overlaps with #2625's data-handling scope.

Deliverables:
- Add a short legal/compliance check to the pre-launch checklist (#2624): privacy policy accuracy vs. actual data handling, and a prompt reminding the builder to check platform ToS before launch (cyber liability insurance is a business/financial decision, not something a code check can verify — note it as a reminder line only, not an automatable check).

Acceptance Criteria:
- The privacy-policy-accuracy check is added as an automatable row (compare policy claims against actual data flows / third-party services used).
- The ToS and insurance items are documented as a manual reminder, not a false-positive-prone automated check.
- Docs cross-reference #2624 and #2625.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DagUP6WjhPx/

groups.title: Add JWT algorithm-confusion checks to the security hardening checklist
groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Current State
A social-media Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed) names a three-point JWT validation check: (1) reject tokens with `alg: none` explicitly, since some JWT libraries accept unsigned tokens by default; (2) enforce the expected signing algorithm server-side, closing the algorithm-confusion attack where an attacker submits an HMAC-signed token using the server's RSA public key as the HMAC secret; (3) always set short token expirations and use a refresh-token flow, since an unexpiring JWT functions as a permanent access key once stolen. This overlaps with, and is meant to extend, the pre-launch security hardening checklist filed as `#2624` (secrets in client bundle, RLS/ownership checks, AI-endpoint auth/rate-limiting) — that record covers authorization and secret-handling gaps but not JWT-specific token-validation attacks. `#2624` itself is currently unbuilt (open, `priority:medium`, no skill implementation exists yet) — there is no live checklist artifact to append rows to today.

## Deliverables
1. Three JWT-validation checklist rows, each with a copy-paste audit prompt matching the pattern `#2624` establishes for its own rows: (a) explicit `alg` allowlist that rejects `none` and any algorithm outside the expected set; (b) server-side enforcement of the expected signing algorithm (rejecting a client-supplied `alg` header value that doesn't match what the server expects to verify with); (c) short-lived access tokens paired with a refresh-token flow, flagging any JWT issued with no expiration or an excessively long one.
2. Documentation of the dependency on `#2624`: if `#2624` ships its checklist/skill first, these three rows get appended directly to it; if this record ships first, it stands alone as an independent JWT-focused checklist file that `#2624`'s eventual implementation is expected to fold in, with an explicit cross-reference in both directions so the two never diverge into duplicate content.
3. A worked example (a sample app snippet or a described scenario) for each of the three checks, demonstrating what a violation looks like, to ground the audit prompt in something a builder can pattern-match against.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Running the `alg: none` check's audit prompt against a sample JWT-verification code path that accepts an unsigned or unexpected-algorithm token flags a violation naming the specific weakness (missing algorithm allowlist).
- Running the algorithm-confusion check's audit prompt against a sample verification path that doesn't pin the expected algorithm server-side (e.g., calls a JWT library's verify function without an explicit `algorithms:` option) flags a violation.
- Running the token-lifetime check's audit prompt against a sample token-issuance path with no expiration claim, or an expiration longer than a stated short-lived threshold, and no refresh-token flow, flags a violation.
- Running all three checks against a sample app that correctly allowlists algorithms, pins the expected algorithm server-side, and issues short-lived tokens with a refresh flow produces no false-positive flags.
- The checklist rows' documentation states explicitly that they extend `#2624` rather than duplicate it, and names the current build-order dependency (which record ships the checklist artifact first).

## Technical Approach
Author the three checklist rows in the same copy-paste-prompt format `#2624`'s own rows use (or will use, once shaped/built), so the two sets of rows are drop-in compatible regardless of build order. Since `#2624` has no shipped skill implementation yet, land these three rows as a standalone markdown checklist file scoped to JWT validation, written so it can be pasted into `#2624`'s eventual body/skill wholesale once that record ships — avoid inventing a separate skill or wrapper mechanism that would need its own maintenance if `#2624`'s checklist becomes a full skill later.

### Key Files
- A new checklist file (path determined by whichever skill or doc structure `#2624`'s implementation adopts, e.g. under `plugin/skills/` if a security-checklist skill is created, or `docs/reference/` if it remains a static checklist) — holds the three JWT-validation rows and their audit prompts.
- `#2624`'s own body/eventual implementation file — cross-reference added in both directions once both records have landed.

## Gotchas
- `#2624` is unbuilt as of this shaping — there is no live checklist artifact today to append rows to. This record may ship first as a standalone JWT checklist; whichever record ships second must fold the other in and add the cross-reference, rather than leaving two independent, silently-diverging checklists.
- The three checks are well-established JWT security practices (each tied to a named, real attack class — unsigned-token acceptance, algorithm confusion, indefinite token validity), so this record is not itself solution-baked, but the exact library-specific audit prompt wording will vary by JWT library (jsonwebtoken, jose, PyJWT, etc.) — the worked examples should name at least one concrete library's API to keep the audit prompt actionable rather than purely abstract.
- Algorithm-confusion attacks specifically require RSA/HMAC key-type mismatch to be exploitable — the audit prompt should clarify this precondition so it doesn't over-flag apps that only ever use a single symmetric algorithm.

## Original request

Add JWT algorithm-confusion checks to the security hardening checklist

Current State:
- Reel (hook-only caption; transcribed) names a three-point JWT check: (1) reject tokens with `alg: none` explicitly — some libraries accept unsigned tokens by default; (2) enforce the expected algorithm server-side so an attacker can't submit an HMAC-signed token using the server's RSA public key as the HMAC secret (algorithm confusion); (3) always set short token expirations and use refresh tokens — an unexpiring JWT is a permanent access key if stolen.
- Overlaps with, and should extend, the pre-launch security checklist already filed as issue #2624 (secrets in client bundle, RLS/ownership checks, AI-endpoint auth/rate-limiting) — this adds the auth-token-validation angle that #2624 doesn't cover.

Deliverables:
- Add the three JWT checks as additional rows on the #2624 checklist (or its eventual skill implementation): explicit `alg` allowlist / reject `none`, enforce expected algorithm server-side, short-lived tokens + refresh flow.
- Ship a copy-paste prompt per check, matching the pipeline's existing pattern.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Running the check against a sample app using JWTs flags a violation in each of the three categories when present.
- Docs note this extends #2624 rather than duplicating it.

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZ71CFgmeVk/

groups.title: Audit skill-authoring guidance for Claude Fable 5.1 prompting deltas
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
claude-tweaks skills are themselves prompts for Claude models, but Anthropic's own official documentation lists behavioral differences for Claude Fable 5.1 vs. 5 (effort-level selection, needing explicit asks for user-facing progress updates, batching independent tool calls, formatting, safeguard false positives, subagent and vision handling) that can silently change how existing skills behave. No skill or CLAUDE.md guidance currently references model-version-specific prompting quirks; skills are written once and assumed stable across model upgrades. Several of the documented deltas (progress-update prompts, tool-call batching) already show up piecemeal in some skill bodies but aren't tracked as a reusable checklist.

## Deliverables
1. Add a short "model-version prompting notes" section or policy row to claude-tweaks' skill-authoring guidance (`docs/skill-authoring.md`, or a cross-reference in `superpowers:writing-skills` if that's where the canonical authoring checklist lives) summarizing the Fable 5.1 deltas that matter for skill instructions: tool-call batching, progress-update prompts, effort-level selection, formatting, safeguard false positives, and subagent/vision handling.
2. Cross-check a sample of existing skills against the documented differences and flag any relying on now-changed default behavior (or confirm none are affected).
3. Link the source doc (Anthropic's Fable 5.1 prompting guide) from the new guidance section so future model version bumps get the same treatment.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The skill-authoring guidance names at least the tool-call-batching, progress-update, and effort-level differences, each with a one-line note on what changed and what a skill author should check for.
2. At least one example skill from the sample cross-check is shown updated against the checklist, or explicitly confirmed unaffected with the reasoning stated.
3. The guidance states this checklist applies whenever a new Claude model version ships, not only for Fable 5.1 — i.e., it's framed as a durable process addition, not a one-off note tied to a single model version.
4. The source doc (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-1) is linked from the new guidance.

## Technical Approach
Add the new "model-version prompting notes" content to `docs/skill-authoring.md` (the canonical skill-authoring conventions file this repo already maintains per CLAUDE.md's Conventions section), phrased as a durable checklist rather than a one-off note about Fable 5.1 specifically. Read a representative sample of existing skills (a mix of frequently-used and complex ones) and check each against the documented deltas — particularly progress-update prompting and tool-call batching, which the record notes already show up piecemeal — noting in the guidance (or as a brief follow-up list) which skills were checked and their outcome.

### Key Files
- `plugin/docs/skill-authoring.md` — add the new model-version prompting notes section/checklist, with the source doc linked
- A sample of existing `plugin/skills/**/SKILL.md` files — read and cross-check against the checklist (exact sample to be chosen at build time; no specific file list mandated by this record)

This record intentionally does not mandate exactly one home for the new guidance ("a short section or policy row... e.g. superpowers:writing-skills or a CLAUDE.md template") — `docs/skill-authoring.md` is the most likely fit given CLAUDE.md's own routing of skill-authoring conventions there, but confirm that's still the canonical location before writing. The cross-check in Deliverable 2/AC2 is a sampling exercise, not an exhaustive audit of every skill file — scope it to a representative handful rather than treating it as a full skill-corpus sweep.
