groups.title: console-execution: no way to resolve a pending-review console answered in chat instead of via PR checkboxes
groups.body:
Surface: terminal

## Current State

`plugin/skills/_shared/console-execution.md`'s "Write order after execution" section (lines 65-81) and its "Live-session accelerator" section (lines 90-107) define a coupled three-write sequence a session must perform once a pending-review console is answered: post a reply comment (`<!-- console-item: executed -->`) summarizing per-item outcomes, edit the console comment's first line to add `<!-- claude-tweaks-console-resolved -->`, then write `console.json.executedAt` and `console.json.resolved: true` together, in one write — strictly in that order (comment marker is the source of truth; `console.json` is the local cache).

When a human present in the dispatching session answers the console by replying in chat ("merge") rather than ticking the PR comment's checkboxes, the "Chat answers first" branch of the Live-session accelerator says to "execute directly ... then perform the same Write order" — but there is no CLI verb or module function that performs those three coupled writes for a session; `bin/lib/reconcile/console-execute.js` exports pure detection/decision functions (`decideConsoleExecute`, `parseItemTicks`, `parseFixesMembers`, etc., all read-only per the file's own "Detection (Node, read-only)" section) but nothing that executes and writes. Every session answering a console this way has to hand-derive the write order from the design notes and reimplement it ad hoc — the exact reverse-engineering this record's Related issue #2544 names as a general problem ("steps prescribed as JS module calls have no CLI verb") applied to this one specific procedure.

`plugin/bin/hooks.js` dispatches subcommands via a flat `cmd = argv[2]` switch (`hooks.js:564`) with a `USAGE`/`KNOWN_FLAGS` table gating `--help` and unknown-flag interception ahead of each mutating verb's own logic (`hooks.js:578-591`) — this is the established pattern any new verb must follow, including the `--run <path>`-required discipline `record-worktree` already enforces (`hooks.js:592-619`) rather than falling back to a guessed "newest non-terminal run."

## Deliverables

1. A new `hooks.js resolve-console --run {run-dir} --approve {ids} --decline {ids}` subcommand that performs the three coupled writes described in `console-execution.md`'s "Write order after execution" section, in the documented order, for a console the calling session (not the reconciler) is resolving after a chat answer.
2. The new verb reuses `console-execute.js`'s existing parsing/decision helpers (`readConsoleJson`, `isResolveTicked`, `parseItemTicks`, `decideConsoleExecute`) rather than re-deriving console state independently — it composes the existing read path with a new write path, not a parallel implementation.
3. `console-execution.md`'s "Live-session accelerator" section is updated to name this verb as the concrete mechanism behind "perform the same Write order," replacing the current prose-only instruction.
4. Registration in `hooks.js`'s `USAGE`/`KNOWN_FLAGS` tables following the `record-worktree` pattern: `--run` is required (no implicit "newest non-terminal run" fallback), and `--help`/unknown-flag interception is wired the same way as every other mutating verb.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `node bin/hooks.js resolve-console --run {run-dir} --approve 1,2,3 --decline 4,5,6` posts exactly one reply comment (`<!-- console-item: executed -->`) summarizing per-item outcomes (executed for approved ids, declined for declined ids), before it edits the console comment's first line to add `<!-- claude-tweaks-console-resolved -->`, before it writes `console.json.executedAt` and `console.json.resolved: true` together in one write — verified by a unit test asserting the three writes happen via an injected fake runner in that exact call order.
- Running the verb with `--run` omitted exits non-zero with a usage message and performs zero writes — no fallback to a guessed run directory, matching `record-worktree`'s existing discipline (`hooks.js:616-619`).
- Running the verb against a console whose `console.json.resolved` is already `true`, or whose `console.json.executingAt` names a live (non-stale) claim, no-ops and reports that state rather than re-executing or re-writing — matching the Idempotence guarantee `console-execution.md`'s "Idempotence" section already documents for the reconciler path.
- Running the verb with an id in `--approve` or `--decline` that does not correspond to any `<!-- console-item: {id} -->` row in the console comment exits non-zero with a clear error naming the unknown id(s), and performs zero writes.
- An item passed in `--decline` is logged as declined with "declined, no reason given" (matching the existing Override-drill decline convention `console-execution.md`'s "Execution routing" section already states), and no execution procedure runs for it.
- A declined `isMergeRow: true` item does not tick the Resolve box on the PR comment if any other item in the console remains unticked, matching the partial-resolution behavior `console-execution.md`'s `consoleAutoResolve` section already describes for a non-floor item.
- `npm test` passes in full after the change, including a new suite exercising the verb's write-order and idempotence behavior via a fake runner (per `gh-api-module-pattern`'s CLI deps contract).
- `plugin/skills/_shared/console-execution.md`'s "Live-session accelerator" section names the new verb explicitly in its "Chat answers first" bullet.

## Technical Approach

Add a `resolve-console` case to `hooks.js`'s `main(argv)` dispatch (alongside the existing `record-worktree` case as the closest structural precedent for a `--run`-required, no-implicit-fallback mutating verb). Parse `--run`, `--approve`, `--decline` via the same `resolveRunArg` helper `record-worktree` uses, requiring `explicit: true` before any write, exactly as `record-worktree` refuses when `--run` is omitted (`hooks.js:616-619`).

Implement the write logic in a new function in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/console-execute.js` (or a sibling module in the same directory, following that file's existing read-only/write split convention) that: (1) reads `console.json` and the PR comment via the same helpers `decideConsoleExecute` already composes; (2) builds the per-item outcome summary from the `--approve`/`--decline` id lists, validating every id against the comment's parsed `<!-- console-item: {id} -->` rows and rejecting unknown ids before any write; (3) posts the reply comment; (4) edits the console comment's first line; (5) writes `console.json.executedAt`/`resolved: true` in one write — strictly in that order, matching `console-execution.md`'s documented Write order.

Route each approved item through the same Execution routing procedures the reconciler path already uses (`execution-and-verification.md`'s apply list, `review-console.md`'s "On approval" steps) — this verb's job is performing the coupled bookkeeping writes and driving that existing routing, not reimplementing item execution.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — add the `resolve-console` case to `main(argv)`'s dispatch, following `record-worktree`'s `--run`-required, no-implicit-fallback pattern (around line 592); register it in the `USAGE`/`KNOWN_FLAGS` tables near the top of the file.
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/console-execute.js` — add the write-performing function that composes the existing read-only helpers (`readConsoleJson`, `isResolveTicked`, `parseItemTicks`, `decideConsoleExecute`) with the new three-step write sequence; export it alongside the existing exports (line 364).
- `plugin/skills/_shared/console-execution.md` — update the "Live-session accelerator" section's "Chat answers first" bullet (around line 97) to name the new verb explicitly instead of the current prose-only "perform the same Write order" instruction.
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/` (or the existing console-execute test file in that directory) — new test coverage for the verb's write order, idempotence, unknown-id rejection, and decline handling, via an injected fake runner.

## Gotchas

- The write order (reply comment → resolved marker → `console.json` fields) is load-bearing for the split-brain repair `console-execution.md`'s "Write order after execution" section describes — a foreign detection pass keys "already executed" off the reply comment's presence, not `console.json` alone. The new verb must preserve this exact order, not just perform the same three writes in any order.
- The pre-execution claim (`console.json.executingAt`/`executingSession`, check-then-act against a 30-minute staleness window) must still be honored by this verb — it is not exempt from the race the reconciler and other live sessions already guard against, per `console-execution.md`'s "Pre-execution claim" section.
- `--approve`/`--decline` id validation must reject ids that don't correspond to any parsed row before performing any write — a partial write followed by an error would leave the console in an inconsistent state.
- The `isMergeRow: true` item's special Resolve-box handling (only ticked when every item in the console is floor-clearing) applies here too — declining any item, including a non-merge one, must leave Resolve unticked per the existing partial-resolution behavior.
- Per `gh-api-module-pattern`'s CLI deps contract, the new write function must take an injectable runner so tests exercise it via a fake runner rather than shelling out to real `gh` calls.

## Original request

console-execution: no way to resolve a pending-review console answered in chat instead of via PR checkboxes

**Summary:** When a dispatched run parks at `pending-review` and the human answers in the dispatching session's chat ("merge") rather than ticking the console comment's checkboxes on the PR, nothing in the plugin can execute and resolve the console: the session has to hand-write the `<!-- console-item: executed -->` reply, tick the executed rows plus Resolve in the console comment, append `<!-- claude-tweaks-console-resolved -->` to its first line, and write `executedAt`/`resolved: true` into `console.json`, in that order, or the reconciler keeps the run at `console-unresolved`.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** _shared/console-execution.md / dispatch Step 6 / wrap-up review-console.md

**Use case:** A human present in the dispatching session wants to approve a parked group's merge (and accept or decline the staged items) by replying in chat, which is how every other console in the plugin is answered. A `hooks.js resolve-console --run {run-dir} --approve 1,2,3 --decline 4,5,6` verb (or a documented in-session procedure that reuses `console-execute.js`'s parsing) would perform the three coupled writes in the documented order and let the normal execution routing run, instead of each session reverse-engineering the write order from the design notes.

**Related:** #2544 (steps prescribed as JS module calls have no CLI verb).

**Definition:** Clear

groups.title: reconcile: archive check tests the main checkout's HEAD, so merged runs stay `local-behind-merge` whenever the main checkout is not on the integration branch
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
Two of `hooks.js reconcile`'s convergence checks assume the main checkout is on the integration branch, and both silently do nothing when it isn't:

1. `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `localHasMerge(root, mergeCommit)` (line 340-346) runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor {mergeCommit.oid} HEAD` in the main checkout — testing whether the merge commit is an ancestor of whatever `HEAD` happens to be, not specifically the integration branch. When the main checkout has a different local branch checked out (e.g. one tracking `origin/develop` under another name), `HEAD` never advances to include the merge, so this check permanently returns `false` and the run is reported `local-behind-merge` indefinitely.
2. `bin/lib/reconcile/mirror-ff.js`'s `mirrorFastForward` (line 40-44) deliberately requires the checked-out branch to equal `integration` before running its `git merge --ff-only origin/{integration}` step — the comment at lines 32-39 explains this is intentional: a bare `git merge` targets whatever's checked out, so merging onto the wrong branch would be silent corruption if that branch also happened to fast-forward cleanly. When the checkout isn't on `integration`, it returns `skipped` with `wrong-branch: checked out on '{x}', not '{integration}'` — a safe choice, but one that means the local integration branch ref never advances either, so `localHasMerge`'s `HEAD`-based test (issue 1) has no path to ever pass.

Together, these two checks combine into a permanent stuck state: every merged run is reported `local-behind-merge` and never archives, for as long as the main checkout stays off the integration branch. The observed workaround was manually running `git fetch origin develop:develop` (updating the local integration branch ref without needing it checked out) followed by `hooks.js close-run` and `hooks.js archive-run` by hand.

## Deliverables
1. `localHasMerge` tests the merge commit's ancestry against the local integration-branch ref (`refs/heads/{integration-branch}`) — or, when that's stale, `origin/{integration-branch}` after a fetch — instead of `HEAD`, so its result no longer depends on what happens to be checked out in the main checkout.
2. `mirrorFastForward` gains a path that updates a non-checked-out local integration branch via `git fetch origin {integration}:{integration}`, which git refuses (loudly) when it wouldn't be a fast-forward — the same safety guarantee `--ff-only` provides today — instead of unconditionally skipping with `wrong-branch` whenever the checkout is on some other branch.
3. The existing `wrong-branch` skip path is preserved as a fallback only when the fetch-based ref update itself isn't viable (e.g. the local integration branch doesn't exist at all yet) — the fix adds a working path for the common case, it doesn't remove the existing safety behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a main checkout with `integration-branch: develop` checked out on a different local branch, and a merged run's commit present on `origin/develop`, `hooks.js reconcile --checks mirror,release,archive` updates the local `develop` ref (via `git fetch origin develop:develop` or equivalent) without needing `develop` checked out.
2. Given the same setup, `localHasMerge` (or its caller) reports the merge commit as present once the local `develop` ref has been updated, using that ref (or `origin/develop`) as the ancestry check target — not `HEAD`.
3. Given the same setup, the merged run's reconcile status advances past `local-behind-merge` (to whatever the next correct state is, e.g. archived) without requiring manual intervention.
4. Given a main checkout actually ON the integration branch (the currently-working case), reconcile's behavior is unchanged — the fix does not alter the already-correct path.
5. Given a local integration-branch ref that would NOT fast-forward cleanly from `origin/{integration}` (a genuine divergence anomaly), the fetch-based update fails loudly (matching `--ff-only`'s existing safety behavior) rather than silently rewriting local history — this is the negative control proving the fix doesn't trade away the existing corruption protection.
6. `mirror-ff.js`'s existing `wrong-branch` skip reason still fires for whatever residual case the fetch-based fix doesn't cover (e.g. no local `develop` ref exists to update), so the fallback behavior remains available rather than removed outright.

## Technical Approach
- In `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`, change `localHasMerge`'s `git merge-base --is-ancestor {oid} HEAD` call to target `refs/heads/{integration}` (or `origin/{integration}` when the local ref is known-stale) instead of `HEAD`. This requires threading the integration branch name into `localHasMerge`'s call sites, since it currently takes only `root` and `mergeCommit`.
- In `bin/lib/reconcile/mirror-ff.js`, add a branch in `mirrorFastForward`'s `'behind'` handling: when `current.stdout !== integration`, attempt `git fetch origin {integration}:{integration}` (a fast-forward-only local ref update by git's own default behavior for that refspec form) before falling back to the existing `wrong-branch` skip. Report the fetch's success/failure the same way the existing `git merge --ff-only` branch does (`fast-forwarded` / `failed` / `skipped`).
- Confirm `git fetch origin {b}:{b}}` genuinely refuses non-fast-forward updates by default (matching `--ff-only`'s safety guarantee) before relying on it — this is the mechanism the record's own workaround already used successfully.
- Update the module-level comments in both files (the `#1130` comment above `localHasMerge`, and the safety-rationale comment above `mirrorFastForward`'s wrong-branch check) to describe the new behavior, since both currently document the old, narrower assumption.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `localHasMerge` (lines 340-346); change ancestry-check target from `HEAD` to the integration-branch ref.
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/mirror-ff.js` — `mirrorFastForward` (lines 15-48); add the fetch-based local-ref-update path for the non-checked-out case, ahead of the existing `wrong-branch` skip.
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/classify.js` — `classifyMirror`, called by `mirrorFastForward`; check whether its own ref comparisons already handle the non-checked-out case correctly (the record's own comment at mirror-ff.js line 32-33 notes `classifyMirror`'s rev-list comparison is "ref-to-ref (safe regardless of what's checked out)" — confirm this holds and that only the write step needs the fix).

## Gotchas
- `mirrorFastForward`'s existing safety rationale (lines 32-39) is well-reasoned: a bare `git merge` on the wrong checked-out branch is silent corruption. The fetch-based fix must preserve an equivalent safety guarantee (fast-forward-only ref update, loud failure on divergence) — do not relax this to a plain `git branch -f` or any other non-ff-safe ref move.
- `localHasMerge`'s caller(s) need to supply the integration branch name; audit every call site to confirm the plumbing is available (likely already resolved elsewhere in the reconcile pipeline via policy resolution) rather than re-deriving it ad hoc.
- Related record #2552 (wrap-up-engine verify's `run-dir-archived`/`reference-repairs`/`plans-ledger` checks failing for reasons outside the run) shares the same root pattern — a check assuming a specific local git state that a legitimate pr-first configuration doesn't guarantee. No shared code between the two records as far as currently known, but worth a final cross-check before closing either.
- The `git fetch origin {b}:{b}` refspec form updates the *local* ref named `{b}` without touching the working tree or index — confirm this doesn't have surprising interactions with a concurrent session that has `{b}` checked out elsewhere (e.g. in a worktree), since fetch-updating a ref that's checked out in another worktree can itself be refused by git; treat that refusal the same as any other `failed` outcome, not a silent no-op.

## Original request

reconcile: archive check tests the main checkout's HEAD, so merged runs stay `local-behind-merge` whenever the main checkout is not on the integration branch

**Summary:** `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `localHasMerge` runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor {mergeCommit} HEAD` in the main checkout. When the main checkout has a differently named local branch checked out (one tracking `origin/develop` under another name), the `mirror` check also skips with `wrong-branch: checked out on '{x}', not 'develop'`, so nothing ever advances HEAD and every merged run is reported `local-behind-merge` and eventually "stuck".

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** bin/lib/reconcile (archive-merged.js localHasMerge, mirror fast-forward)

**Repro steps:**
1. `integration-branch: develop`, `integration-model: pr-first`; main checkout checked out on a local branch that is not `develop`.
2. Merge a run's PR; run `hooks.js reconcile --checks mirror,release,archive`.
3. Observe `mirror: skipped wrong-branch` and the run `skipped: local-behind-merge`; repeat forever.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the archive check compares against the local integration-branch ref (`refs/heads/{integration-branch}`) or `origin/{integration-branch}` after a fetch, and the mirror fast-forward updates a non-checked-out local integration branch with `git fetch origin {b}:{b}` instead of skipping.
Actual: permanently stuck; workaround was `git fetch origin develop:develop` plus `hooks.js close-run` and `hooks.js archive-run` by hand.

**Related:** #2552 (wrap-up-engine verify's run-dir-archived check fails for reasons outside the run).

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.126.0

groups.title: Plugin commit call sites have no bounded git index.lock retry, so a sibling agent's git call fails a reconcile or release step
groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #1728, #1734, #1738, #1811, #1826, #1841, #1892, #1982, #2032, #2051, #2081, #2226, #2228, #2229, #2230, #2231, #2240, #2330, #2332 (near-duplicate screen hits — shared file-path/anchor mentions only, not confirmed duplicates of this record's own topic)

## Current State

In one seven-spec multi-record run, eight commits failed with
`fatal: Unable to create '<repo>/.git/index.lock': File exists`. The lock holder was a sibling
agent's git call or a PostToolUse hook in the same checkout, never a stale process — every one of
them succeeded on a retry a couple of seconds later. The run only got through because the ad-hoc
ledger-append scripts written for it grew their own 2-second retry loop; nothing in the plugin
provided one.

The plugin's own commit call sites run `git commit` through `execFileSync` with no retry at all:

- `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `runGit(['commit', '-m', '[reconcile] archive run …'])`
- `bin/lib/release/run.js` — `deps.git(['commit', '-m', 'Release v… — …'])`
- `bin/release-local.js` — `deps.git(['commit', '-m', 'chore(release): v…'])`

A transient index-lock collision at any of these surfaces as a hard failure of a reconcile or
release step, in exactly the multi-agent setting the plugin is built for (parallel dispatch,
worktrees, hooks running git in the background). The sanctioned run-dir writers
(`log-decision.js`, `stage-item.js`, `set-config.js`) never take the index lock and are unaffected;
`bin/lib/file-lock.js` is a directory mutex for file stores, not git's index.

The precedent for the exact shape already exists one directory over:
`bin/lib/feedback/file-feedback.js`'s `withTransientRetry(runner, { waitMs, maxRetries, sleep })`
(confirmed, line 70) wraps `gh` calls on a transient-error signature, with an injectable `sleep` so
tests do not wait. Nothing equivalent guards git. A standing memory entry already records the
operator-side rule for this failure ("retry, never `rm` the lock"); the plugin's own code does not
follow it.

## Deliverables

- A shared bounded retry for index-lock contention — `bin/lib/git-retry.js` exporting
  `withIndexLockRetry(gitRunner, { attempts, waitMs, sleep })`, shaped like
  `withTransientRetry`: retry **only** on a stderr signature naming `index.lock`
  (`Unable to create … index.lock` / `another git process seems to be running`), bounded
  (~15 attempts at 2 s), injectable `sleep`, and never unlinking a lock file.
- Route every plugin commit call site through it: `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`,
  `bin/lib/release/run.js`, `bin/release-local.js`.
- State the rule once where skill prose instructs a commit, so a hand-written commit path
  retries the same way instead of each script growing its own loop, and cite it rather than
  restating it (CLAUDE.md's cross-reference rule).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `withIndexLockRetry` retries on an `index.lock` stderr signature and does **not** retry on any
   other git failure — both directions asserted with a fake runner (a fake failing on
   `index.lock` twice then succeeding produces one commit and no error; a fake failing on an
   unrelated git error fails on the first attempt).
2. The helper never unlinks a lock file — asserted directly, not merely absent from the source.
3. Retries are bounded: a fake runner that always fails on `index.lock` exits after the configured
   attempt count with the original git error, and the injected `sleep` makes the test instant.
4. Each of the three named commit call sites routes through the helper (grep proves no direct
   `['commit', …]` call bypasses it), and `npm test` passes.

## Non-Goals

- Replacing the sanctioned run-dir writers' `file-lock.js` mutex; it guards a different resource.
- Any change to what the commits contain or when they run — only how a transient lock is survived.

## Technical Approach

Model `bin/lib/git-retry.js`'s `withIndexLockRetry` directly on the existing
`withTransientRetry` pattern in `bin/lib/feedback/file-feedback.js:70` — same shape (a wrapping
higher-order function taking a runner and an options object with an injectable `sleep`), but
keyed on a different error signature: match stderr for `index.lock` or `another git process seems
to be running` rather than `file-feedback.js`'s own transient-`gh`-error signature. Wrap each of
the three named call sites' `git(['commit', ...])` invocation with it, passing each site's
existing runner through unchanged — this is a call-site wrapping, not a rewrite of any of the
three modules' own commit logic. Then find wherever skill prose (a `SKILL.md` or `_shared/*.md`
file) instructs an agent to run `git commit` directly as part of a documented procedure, and add
one citation to this new shared retry rule there (per this codebase's cross-reference convention:
state the rule once, cite it everywhere) rather than restating the retry logic in prose at each
site.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/git-retry.js` — new file, `withIndexLockRetry` (model on
  `bin/lib/feedback/file-feedback.js`'s `withTransientRetry`)
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — route its `commit` call through the new retry
- `plugin/bin/lib/release/run.js` — route its `commit` call through the new retry
- `plugin/bin/release-local.js` — route its `commit` call through the new retry
- A skill/`_shared/*.md` file instructing a hand-written `git commit` in prose — add one citation
  to the new rule (exact file identified via a grep at build time)

## Gotchas

- Never unlink the lock file — this is an explicit, tested requirement (Acceptance Criterion 2),
  not an incidental detail; a standing memory entry in this repo records this as the
  operator-side rule the plugin's own code is catching up to.
- Match the retry signature narrowly (`index.lock` / "another git process seems to be running")
  — a broad transient-error match would risk silently retrying a genuine, non-lock git failure
  and masking it behind a multi-attempt delay.
- The sanctioned run-dir writers (`log-decision.js`, `stage-item.js`, `set-config.js`) are
  explicitly out of scope — they use a different lock mechanism (`file-lock.js`, a directory
  mutex) for a different resource, and don't take git's index lock at all.

groups.title: archive-merged.js: work-twin-conflict failure reasons never escalate to residue tracking
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`.
New failure reasons `work-twin-conflict` (confirmed, ~line 684) and
`work-twin-resolve-failed[-partial-revert]` are never tracked toward residue escalation, so a
genuinely diverged work twin is skipped silently on every reconcile pass forever — no streak, no
issue filed.

`trackArchiveResult` (confirmed, ~line 1083) early-returns `if (result.reason !== 'move-failed')
return;` before reaching `trackResidue`, and `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (confirmed, line 1030)
is `new Set(['no-worktree', 'no-branch', 'no-pr'])` — it doesn't include either new twin reason.

## Deliverables

Extend `trackArchiveResult`/`STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (or add an equivalent path) so a
`work-twin-conflict`/`work-twin-resolve-failed[-partial-revert]` result accumulates toward the
same residue-escalation streak as the existing structurally-stuck reasons, rather than being
silently dropped every pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

A reconcile run that repeatedly hits `work-twin-conflict` on the same run dir eventually
escalates (streak-based issue filing), the same way a repeated `no-worktree`/`no-branch`/`no-pr`
result does today.

## Technical Approach

Widen `trackArchiveResult`'s early-return guard (~line 1083) from the single literal
`result.reason !== 'move-failed'` to also accept `work-twin-conflict` and
`work-twin-resolve-failed`/`work-twin-resolve-failed-partial-revert`, routing them into the same
`trackResidue(root, repoSlug, {reason}, dir, { failed: true, lastError: result.lastError },
{ escalate })` call the `move-failed` path already uses — reuse the existing choke point rather
than duplicating escalation logic. Decide whether the twin reasons need their own `reason` key
passed to `trackResidue` (distinct from `'move-failed'`) so `escalate-residue.js`'s filed-issue
title/body correctly names "work-twin-conflict" rather than generically reusing "move-failed" —
this affects how a human reading the escalated issue understands what actually went wrong, so
prefer the more specific reason string.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — widen `trackArchiveResult`'s reason guard
  (~line 1083) to also route `work-twin-conflict`/`work-twin-resolve-failed[-partial-revert]`
  into `trackResidue`

## Gotchas

- `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (line 1030) governs a *different* mechanism (the
  `isStructurallyStuck()`/`no-branch`-class TTL-based staleness check) than
  `trackArchiveResult`'s own `move-failed`-keyed residue tracking — don't conflate the two; this
  record's fix is about routing the twin reasons into `trackResidue`'s escalation streak, not
  necessarily adding them to `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` itself (which governs a specific,
  separate no-worktree/no-branch/no-pr classification). Verify which mechanism actually needs
  the new reasons before changing both.
- A `work-twin-resolve-failed-partial-revert` is a worse state than a clean `work-twin-conflict`
  (a partially-applied revert) — make sure the escalated issue's body can distinguish the two
  reasons, not just lump them under one generic label, since a human resolving the escalation
  needs to know which situation they're looking at.

## Original request

## Current State
Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`. New failure reasons `work-twin-conflict` and `work-twin-resolve-failed[-partial-revert]` (~line 684) are never tracked toward residue escalation, so a genuinely diverged work twin is skipped silently on every reconcile pass forever — no streak, no issue filed.

`trackArchiveResult` (~line 1076) early-returns `if (result.reason !== 'move-failed') return;` before reaching `trackResidue`, and `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (~line 1023) is `{'no-worktree','no-branch','no-pr'}` — it doesn't include either new twin reason.

## Deliverables
Extend `trackArchiveResult`/`STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (or add an equivalent path) so a `work-twin-conflict`/`work-twin-resolve-failed[-partial-revert]` result accumulates toward the same residue-escalation streak as the existing structurally-stuck reasons, rather than being silently dropped every pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
A reconcile run that repeatedly hits `work-twin-conflict` on the same run dir eventually escalates (streak-based issue filing), the same way a repeated `no-worktree`/`no-branch`/`no-pr` result does today.

groups.title: hooks.js hardcodes one bespoke recovery message for archive-merged's audit-untracked reason, generic for ~15 others
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/bin/hooks.js`'s `archive-run` verb prints the result of `archiveRunDir(mainRoot, runDir)`. One reason gets a bespoke six-line recovery message, selected by `if (result.reason === 'audit-untracked')` and interpolating `result.untrackedAuditFiles`; every other refusal prints `claude-tweaks: archival refused — {reason}`. `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` produces fourteen distinct reason codes (`move-failed`, `readdir-failed`, `mkdir-failed`, `console-unresolved`, `console-never-rendered`, `tracked-entry`, `no-pr`, `no-branch`, `network-failure`, `ls-files-failed`, `gh-absent`, `close-write-failed`, `close-failed`, `audit-untracked`, plus `git-mv-failed`/`git-mv-failed-partial-revert`) as ad hoc `{ ok: false, reason, … }` literals, some with extra fields (`lastError`, `untrackedAuditFiles`) that only the dispatcher knows to read. The recovery knowledge for `audit-untracked` lives 400 lines away from the code that detects it, and a rename of the reason code in `archive-merged.js` would silently downgrade the message to the generic line — nothing pins the two together. `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` asserts the message text (`archival refused — audit-untracked`, `sync this checkout with origin`), so the text can move but not change.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `archive-merged.js` gains one refusal constructor, `refusal(reason, { hint = null, ...extra } = {})` → `{ ok: false, reason, hint, ...extra }`, and every `{ ok: false, reason: … }` literal in the file goes through it, so each result carries a `hint` key (string or `null`) beside its reason.
- [ ] The `audit-untracked` recovery text moves verbatim from `hooks.js` into that refusal's `hint`, built where `untrackedAuditFiles` is computed; `move-failed` and the two `git-mv-failed*` refusals set `hint` from `lastError` when present; the other codes start with `hint: null` (no invented prose).
- [ ] `hooks.js`'s `archive-run` branch drops the `reason === 'audit-untracked'` match and prints `claude-tweaks: archival refused — {reason}` followed, when `result.hint` is a non-empty string, by ` — {hint}`; the exit code and the `moved:` lines are unchanged.
- [ ] A conformance test that every `reason: '…'` literal in `archive-merged.js` sits inside a `refusal(` call (a source scan), and unit cases that `refusal` always yields a `hint` key and that the `audit-untracked` result's hint names its files.
- [ ] `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` passes unmodified (its regexes match the moved text); `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` cases that deep-equal a refusal object are updated only to include `hint: null` where they assert whole objects.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `hooks.js` contains no comparison against a specific `archive-merged.js` reason string; the `archive-run` branch reads only `ok`, `reason`, `hint`, and `movedEntries`.
2. `node bin/hooks.js archive-run` on the untracked-audit fixture prints the same `audit-untracked` sentence as today (the existing test's regexes are the proof); every other refusal prints its reason exactly as today, with a hint appended only where one was set.
3. Every refusal object `archiveRunDir` and its helpers return has a `hint` property; the source scan finds no bare `{ ok: false, reason:` literal outside `refusal`.
4. `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Co-locate the story with the detector, keep the dispatcher dumb: a `hint` field is the smallest contract change that lets the next non-obvious failure ship its recovery text without a new `if` in `hooks.js`, and a constructor is what makes "every refusal has the field" a source-scannable invariant rather than a convention. Hints stay `null` for the codes whose one-line reason already says what happened (`gh-absent`, `no-pr`); writing prose for all fourteen would be the speculative work the record warns against. The `console-*` and `network-failure` codes come from `decideArchive`'s pure skip path (`{ action: 'skip', reason }`), which is a different shape consumed inside the loop, not by `hooks.js` — leave it alone and say so in the constructor's comment.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `archiveRunDir`, `archiveOrphanedMint`, `revertWorkMoves`/`revertPlainMoves`, the `audit-untracked` branch (`untrackedAuditFiles`), every `ok: false` literal.
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js` — the `archive-run` verb's refusal printing.
- `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js` — text pins (unchanged); `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — object-shape cases.

## Gotchas
- The `audit-untracked` sentence is asserted by regex in `tests/archive-run-verb.test.js`; move it character-for-character, including the `git pull, or reconcile's own mirror-ff` clause.
- `trackArchiveResult` in the same file consumes `result.reason` and `result.lastError` for residue tracking; adding `hint` must not change what it reads, and `lastError` stays as its own field rather than being folded into `hint`.
- #1732 (classifier) and #1733 (loop extraction) touch the same file; this record touches only the refusal literals and can land before or after either, but never in parallel with them.
- Do not print hints for `dryRun` skips: `archiveMerged`'s `skipped` entries are a different consumer and the reconcile report renders them itself.

## Original request

`plugin/bin/hooks.js` has a single hardcoded `if (result.reason === 'audit-untracked')` branch that prints a bespoke multi-line recovery message, while `archive-merged.js`'s ~15 other reason codes (`mkdir-failed`, `git-mv-failed`, `ls-files-failed`, `tracked-entry`, `commit-failed`, ...) all fall through to a generic one-line message. The rich, actionable recovery text lives in the CLI dispatcher rather than co-located with the code that understands the failure, and nothing keeps a renamed/removed reason code in `archive-merged.js` in sync with this dispatcher-side string match.


Defer-reason: genuinely-larger — touches the reason-code contract across archive-merged.js's ~15 failure paths and its hooks.js dispatcher, not a localized change; found by the pre-v6.117.0 whole-branch review.

groups.title: reconcile: worktree reap fails with "Filename too long" on Windows and leaves the worktree prunable
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State
After a merge, `bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` attempts to remove the run's worktree via `git worktree remove`. On Windows, a pnpm/Node monorepo worktree under `.claude/worktrees/{worktree}` with installed `node_modules` frequently has deep nested paths that exceed Windows's `MAX_PATH` limit, causing `git worktree remove` to fail with `Filename too long`. Git partially unregisters the worktree in this failure case, leaving it in a `prunable` state while the directory remains on disk. `reap-merged.js` reports this as `worktrees: [{ action: "skipped", reason: "removal-failed" }]` and leaves cleanup to a human — the observed workaround was a small ad-hoc Node script using the `\\?\` long-path prefix with `fs.rmSync`, followed by `git worktree prune` and `git branch -D`. Related: #1796 (escalate-residue's removal-failed escalation body), which currently handles this failure by escalating to a human rather than attempting the long-path fallback.

## Deliverables
1. In `bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js`, when `git worktree remove` fails, add a fallback: `fs.rmSync('\\\\?\\' + path, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries })` (the `\\?\` long-path prefix bypasses Windows's `MAX_PATH` limit), followed by `git worktree prune`, then the branch delete step that would otherwise have run after a successful `git worktree remove`.
2. Confirm this fallback is a no-op / behaves correctly on non-Windows platforms (the `\\?\` prefix is Windows-specific; the fallback should only trigger after a genuine removal failure, and should not be reached at all on platforms where `git worktree remove` already succeeds for long paths).
3. Update #1796's removal-failed escalation body (or confirm no update needed) to reflect that a long-path fallback is now attempted before escalating to a human — the escalation should now only fire if the fallback itself also fails.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On Windows, a worktree removal that fails with `Filename too long` due to deep `node_modules` paths is retried via the `\\?\`-prefixed `fs.rmSync` fallback, and this fallback succeeds where the direct `git worktree remove` failed — verified with a reproduction fixture (a worktree containing a deeply nested path exceeding `MAX_PATH`) or, if a live Windows CI runner isn't available, a unit test that mocks `git worktree remove`'s failure and asserts the fallback's `fs.rmSync` call receives the correctly prefixed path.
- After the fallback succeeds, `git worktree prune` runs and the worktree no longer appears as `prunable` in `git worktree list`, and the branch delete step (that would run after a normal successful removal) also completes.
- `reap-merged.js`'s existing `removal-failed` escalation (per #1796) still fires when the fallback itself fails (e.g. permissions issue unrelated to path length), so a genuine unrecoverable failure is still surfaced to a human rather than silently swallowed.
- No behavior change on non-Windows platforms where `git worktree remove` already succeeds — verified by the existing `reap-merged.js` test suite continuing to pass unmodified for the success-path cases.

## Technical Approach
Add the long-path fallback directly in `reap-merged.js`'s worktree-removal step, gated behind the `git worktree remove` failure branch (not gated behind `process.platform === 'win32'` alone, since the fallback should simply be attempted whenever the primary removal fails — the `\\?\` prefix is a no-op/harmless on paths that don't need it, though confirm this assumption or gate by platform if it isn't safe cross-platform). Reuse `maxRetries`/`recursive`/`force` options already established as conventions elsewhere in this codebase's filesystem-cleanup code, if any exist, rather than inventing new retry semantics.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` — add the long-path `fs.rmSync` fallback after a `git worktree remove` failure, followed by `git worktree prune` and the branch delete
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/` (escalate-residue module, per #1796) — confirm/update the removal-failed escalation body to reflect the new fallback-before-escalate ordering

## Gotchas
- Confirm the `\\?\` long-path prefix is safe to prepend unconditionally (i.e., doesn't break `fs.rmSync` on macOS/Linux where the prefix has no meaning) before deciding whether to gate this fallback by `process.platform === 'win32'` or apply it universally.
- `git worktree prune` after a manual `fs.rmSync` removal must run correctly even though the directory was removed by Node rather than by git itself — verify prune correctly detects the now-missing directory and cleans up git's internal worktree registration.
- This is a defect specific to Windows long-path behavior; without Windows CI, verification may need to rely on a mocked/simulated failure path rather than a genuine reproduction — call this out explicitly in the PR/build notes if a live Windows repro isn't available.

## Original request

reconcile: worktree reap fails with "Filename too long" on Windows and leaves the worktree prunable

**Summary:** After a merge, `bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` reports `removal-failed` for the run's worktree because `git worktree remove` fails on Windows with `Filename too long` (deep `node_modules` paths); git unregisters part of the worktree, leaving it `prunable` with the directory still on disk.

**Repro steps:**

2. Merge the worktree's PR; run `hooks.js reconcile`.
3. Observe `worktrees: [{ action: "skipped", reason: "removal-failed" }]` and `git worktree list` showing the entry as `prunable`.

Actual: left for a human; workaround was a small Node script with the long-path prefix plus `git worktree prune` and `git branch -D`.

groups.title: escalate-residue: removal-failed escalation body names the plugin's own path as the fix site and omits the worktree's dirty-file list
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`residueBody` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.js`) composes every reconcile escalation issue — `removal-failed`, `structurally-stuck`, `move-failed` — from `{reason, targetPath, count, firstFailedAt, lastError}` and ends with the literal line ``Filed automatically by `bin/lib/reconcile` — see #644.``. In a consumer project that line reads as a repo-relative path and a local issue number: neither exists there, and `/claude-tweaks:specify`'s shaping sanity check has no way to know the path belongs to the plugin. Three consumer records were shaped with `bin/lib/reconcile/` as their Key File and each failed a headless build on "named location does not exist" before being closed as upstream.

For `removal-failed`, `reap-merged.js`'s failure branch (`if (rm.failure)`) forwards only `rm.stderr || rm.failure` as `lastError` (#1341) into `trackReapResidue` → `cache.js`'s `trackResidue`/`recordResidueFailure` (which persists `{count, firstFailedAt, lastError, escalated}` per `reason:path`) → `escalateResidue`. Git's refusal text ("contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it") says the worktree is dirty but not *with what*; the reader cannot tell a leftover untracked ledger from real uncommitted work without shelling into the host. `bin/lib/residue/probes/worktrees.js`'s `defaultIsDirty` already runs `git -C {path} status --porcelain` (10 s timeout, `null` on read failure), but reduces the output to a boolean and is not called from the reaper.

Tests: `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.test.js` (six cases; "residueBody: embeds the path, reason, and the fingerprint marker"), `reap-merged.test.js`, `cache.test.js`. Related, distinct: #1424 (tidy path: never classify a dirty worktree as deletable), #1341 (the human handoff this body implements), #1811 and #1892 (this sweep's consolidated `structurally-stuck`/`move-failed` records for this repo's own residue; both keep `bin/lib/reconcile/` as a correct Key File *here*).

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Attribution line that survives a consumer repo.** Replace the closing line in `residueBody` with one that names the code owner and the record's purpose for all three reasons: filed by the claude-tweaks plugin's reconcile pass; the logic lives in the plugin source (`bin/lib/reconcile/` of `thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks`, not a path in this repository); a fix to the reconcile logic belongs upstream (`thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks#644` as the tracking reference, fully qualified); this record is the human handoff for the path named above. Keep the fingerprint marker and its basis unchanged so existing dedup keeps matching.
- [ ] **Carry the dirty-file list on `removal-failed`.** In `reap-merged.js`'s failure branch, read `git -C {real} status --porcelain` (extract `worktrees.js`'s porcelain read into a small exported helper that returns the raw lines or `null`, and have `defaultIsDirty` call it, so there is one implementation) and pass `dirtyFiles` (array of porcelain lines, capped at 50 with a `… and N more` tail line) through `trackReapResidue` → `trackResidue` → `recordResidueFailure` (persist `dirtyFiles` next to `lastError`, refreshed on every failure, dropped with the streak on success) → `escalateResidue` → `residueBody`, which renders a `**Dirty files (\`git status --porcelain\` at the last failed pass):**` fenced block. When the read returned `null`, render `could not read — git status failed` in that block rather than omitting it (a check that did not run must not look like a clean worktree).
- [ ] **Disposition hint, no behavior change to the reaper.** Below the block, one line: only `??` (untracked) entries that are plainly disposable make `git worktree remove --force {path}` safe; any modified tracked entry means inspect first. The reaper itself never gains `--force` (the original request's explicit non-goal).
- [ ] **Tests.** `escalate-residue.test.js`: attribution line names the plugin and the qualified upstream ref, no bare `bin/lib/reconcile` path; `dirtyFiles` block rendered, capped, and the `null` case rendered as unreadable; non-`removal-failed` reasons render no block. `reap-merged.test.js`: on `rm.failure` the porcelain read runs against the worktree path and its lines reach the injected `escalate`. `cache.test.js`: `dirtyFiles` persisted and replaced per failure, cleared on success. `tests/bin-lib/residue/*`: `defaultIsDirty` still returns `true`/`false`/`null` through the shared helper.
- [ ] Update `docs/reconcile-checks.md` if it quotes the body's closing line or the cache entry shape (grep first; edit only the quoted text).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `residueBody({reason: 'structurally-stuck', …}).body` contains the plugin attribution with `thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks#644` and does not contain the bare line ``Filed automatically by `bin/lib/reconcile` ``; the fingerprint marker is byte-identical to today's for the same `(reason, path)`.
2. `residueBody({reason: 'removal-failed', dirtyFiles: ['?? docs/plans/x-ledger.md']}).body` contains a fenced block with that line and the disposition hint; with `dirtyFiles: null` it contains the unreadable sentence; with 60 lines it renders 50 plus a `… and 10 more` tail.
3. In `reap-merged.test.js`, a failed `git worktree remove` results in exactly one `status --porcelain` invocation against the worktree path and the lines appear on the escalation call's arguments; a successful removal performs no status read.
4. `cache.json`'s `residueFailures[reason:path]` entry carries `dirtyFiles` after a failure and the entry is deleted on success, pinned in `cache.test.js`.
5. `npm test` green; every pre-existing case in the three reconcile test files and in `tests/bin-lib/residue/` passes unchanged.
6. A record filed by this code in a consumer repo, shaped by `/claude-tweaks:specify`, would not name `bin/lib/reconcile/` as a Key File — demonstrated in the PR description by quoting the new body text and stating which sentence carries the upstream pointer.

## Technical Approach

Additive: a new optional `dirtyFiles` field on the cache entry and the escalation call, `null`/absent for the two other reasons, so no existing consumer changes shape. One porcelain reader shared between the residue probe and the reaper, with the same 10 s timeout and `null`-on-failure contract. The attribution rewrite is text only; keep the marker line last so `tidy-residue-markers` style consumers that locate the fingerprint keep working. Cap the list in the reaper, not in the body composer, so the cache never stores an unbounded array.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.js` — attribution line; `dirtyFiles` block + hint in `residueBody`; pass-through in `escalateResidue`
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js` — porcelain read on `rm.failure`; `dirtyFiles` into `trackReapResidue`
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js` — persist `dirtyFiles` in `recordResidueFailure`; forward it in `trackResidue`'s `escalate` call
- `plugin/bin/lib/residue/probes/worktrees.js` — export the porcelain reader `defaultIsDirty` now delegates to
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.test.js`, `reap-merged.test.js`, `cache.test.js` — new cases
- `docs/reconcile-checks.md` — only if it quotes the closing line or the cache entry shape

## Gotchas

- The reconcile pass runs in the background on every session (`reconcile-background.lock`); a status read on a dirty worktree is one more spawn per failed reap — bounded by the 10 s timeout and only on the failure branch, so acceptable, but do not add it to the success path.
- Porcelain lines can contain paths with spaces and renames (`R  old -> new`); store them verbatim, never split.
- Do not change the fingerprint basis: an attribution change must not re-file already-escalated paths.
- Records this code already filed in this repo (the `structurally-stuck`/`move-failed` instances absorbed into #1811 and #1892 by this sweep) keep their old body text; nothing here rewrites filed issues.

## Original request

**Summary:** A `removal-failed` escalation issue filed by `bin/lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.js` reads, in the consumer project, as an in-repo bug ("Filed automatically by `bin/lib/reconcile` — see #644") and carries git's stderr but not the dirty worktree's `git status --porcelain` output — so a human cannot tell a disposable untracked ledger from real uncommitted work without visiting the host, and a downstream `/specify` shapes the record with `bin/lib/reconcile/` as its Key File even though that directory does not exist in the consumer repo.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/lib/reconcile/escalate-residue.js` (`residueBody`), with `bin/lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js`'s `removal-failed` tracking as the producer

**Repro steps:**
1. In a consumer project (not claude-tweaks itself), let a merged-PR worktree accumulate one untracked file (e.g. a leftover `docs/plans/*-ledger.md`) so `git worktree remove` refuses with `contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it`.
2. Let reconcile's reap pass hit `removal-failed` on that path three times so `cache.js`'s escalation latch trips and `escalateResidue` files the issue.
3. Read the filed issue body, then run `/claude-tweaks:specify #N` on it.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the body says the removal logic lives in the claude-tweaks plugin (a fix, if any, belongs upstream — and a maintainer reading the consumer's issue should not be pointed at a repo-relative `bin/lib/reconcile/`), and it lists the worktree's porcelain lines so the reader can decide between "disposable residue — `git worktree remove --force` is safe" and "real uncommitted work — inspect first" without shelling into the host. `bin/lib/residue/probes/worktrees.js` already has `isDirty(worktreePath)` running `git status --porcelain`; `residueBody` only needs the porcelain text, not just the boolean.
Actual: the body's fix-site line reads as a consumer-repo path (three reconcile-filed records were shaped by `/specify` with `bin/lib/reconcile/` as Key File and each failed a headless build on "named location does not exist" before being closed as unreproducible/upstream), and the body's only diagnostic is git's one-line stderr. This is the escalation-path half of what claude-tweaks #1424 fixed for the `/tidy` path (never classify a dirty worktree as deletable, never offer bare `--force`) and the human handoff #1341 designed — the handoff works, it just does not carry the one fact the human needs. Not a request to add `--force` to the reaper.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.0

groups.title: specify: never emit a /claude-tweaks:feedback-filing deliverable for a component the spec itself places outside the plugin
groups.body:
## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:specify` can materialize a spec whose own `## Current State` / `## Technical
Approach` section correctly identifies the affected component as living outside the plugin (a
third-party dependency, or in this case the Claude Code harness itself) — and still carry a
Deliverable/Acceptance-Criterion directing `/claude-tweaks:feedback` to file an upstream report
against that component. `feedback/SKILL.md`'s own scope line is explicit: "Do not use this skill
to file against any repository other than `thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks`." — and
`learning-routing.md`'s classifier would route a genuine harness/dependency quirk with no owning
claude-tweaks artifact to D4 (memory) or D2 (project doc), never D5, since D5 requires the learning
to name a `/claude-tweaks:*` skill, a `skills/_shared/*` contract, or a `bin/*.js` behavior. A spec
that both correctly diagnoses "this is not ours" and then asks for a `/claude-tweaks:feedback`
filing anyway is internally contradictory.

Reproduced by #1785 (materialized 2026-09-14): its `## Current State` explicitly corrects the
originally-filed attribution ("The record as filed attributes the guard to
`bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`. That attribution is wrong ... this is harness behavior"), yet its
Deliverables still directed: "File one upstream report through `/claude-tweaks:feedback` targeting
the Claude Code harness." That deliverable is structurally unreachable — `/claude-tweaks:feedback`
Step 2 would itself stop ("If it is not D5, stop") before ever reaching Step 3's self-reference
check. The build's own SDD fix-loop noticed the filing couldn't happen but reasoned it via an
inapplicable self-reference collapse (which only fires for a learning that already reached D5)
rather than catching that the learning never qualified as D5 in the first place.

## Deliverables

- Add a check to `/claude-tweaks:specify`'s spec-composition step (wherever a "Suggested change"
  from an `## Original request` becomes a Deliverable naming `/claude-tweaks:feedback`): before
  emitting a feedback-filing Deliverable, run the same classification `learning-routing.md`'s
  classifier and `feedback/SKILL.md` Step 2 would apply — does the record's own Current State /
  affected-component analysis place the subject inside the plugin (a `/claude-tweaks:*` skill,
  `skills/_shared/*` contract, or `bin/*.js` behavior)? If not, never emit the feedback-filing
  Deliverable/AC.
- When the check fails, route the spec's language instead per `learning-routing.md`'s own
  Non-claude-tweaks-upstream paragraph ("Report it to the user, name the owner, and stop") or its
  D4/D2 outcome — whichever this repo's spec-authoring convention should surface as — rather than
  silently omitting the concern.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A spec whose Current State / Technical Approach already identifies the affected component as
  outside the plugin (third-party harness, dependency, or corrected mis-attribution) never carries
  a Deliverable or Acceptance Criterion directing `/claude-tweaks:feedback` to file against that
  component.
- `/claude-tweaks:specify`'s own spec-shape validation (or a `/claude-tweaks:challenge` lens) catches
  this class of solution-baked, unfileable deliverable before the spec reaches `ready`.
- Regression case: re-run `/claude-tweaks:specify` against a record shaped like #1785 (an originally
  mis-attributed harness quirk, corrected in the same spec) and confirm no feedback-filing
  Deliverable is emitted.

_Filed by `capture` via specShapedBody, discovered during #1785 review._

groups.title: bin/verify.js: only one reserved "types" check name, but a monorepo can have N independent typecheck commands
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`bin/verify.js` (the shared `/claude-tweaks:test` and `/claude-tweaks:build` verification
runner) reserves only one `"types"` check name for the fail-fast-before-tests tier, alongside
`"lint"` — confirmed by grep: the literal strings `'types'`/`'lint'` are hardcoded at multiple
points (`verify.js:212`'s `allowed` set, `:265`'s static-check branch, `:281`'s `staticNames`
filter, `:387` and `:451`'s `suitesRun` filters). A monorepo can have multiple independent
typecheck commands with no way to give more than one that treatment.

A pnpm/npm workspace monorepo with multiple independently-typed packages (e.g. three packages
each needing their own `tsc --noEmit`, with no single command that covers all three) wants
typecheck and lint to run independently of whether `tests` happens to pass. Naming the extra
typecheck commands something else (e.g. `types-core`, `types-worker`, `types-web`) demotes them
to the "any other name" tier, which runs serially **after** `tests` succeeds under the same
fail-fast policy — so when `tests` fails for a reason unrelated to any of the typechecks (e.g. a
flaky test-hook timeout under concurrent machine load), all three typechecks get skipped
(`skipped: fail-fast`) even though none of them actually depend on `tests` passing. A caller then
has to notice the `skipped: fail-fast` rows and re-run each typecheck command by hand, outside
the runner, to get a real signal.

Reproduction: `node bin/verify.js --cmd types-core="..." --cmd types-worker="..." --cmd
types-web="..." --cmd lint="..." --cmd tests="..."` where `tests` fails for any reason —
`report.json` shows `types-core`/`types-worker`/`types-web` as `{"skipped": "fail-fast"}` even
though each is independent of `tests`.

## Deliverables

Choose and implement one of:

- **(a) Widen the reserved tier**: let multiple checks share the reserved pre-`tests` tier — e.g.
  any `--cmd` name prefixed `types:` or `types-` joins the same concurrent-with-lint,
  fail-fast-before-tests group the single `types` name gets today. This requires updating every
  hardcoded `'types'`/`'lint'` comparison site (`verify.js:212`, `:265`, `:281`, `:387`, `:451`)
  to a prefix-match instead of an exact-string match.
- **(b) Document the workaround**: explicitly document that a monorepo with N independent
  typecheck commands should invoke them as their own `verify.js` call, or combine them into one
  compound `--cmd types="a && b && c"`, rather than as N separately-named checks — so the
  fail-fast-skip behavior is expected rather than surprising.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Whichever option is chosen, a monorepo with multiple independent typecheck commands has a
  documented, working path to get fail-fast-before-tests treatment for all of them (not just one
  named `types`) — either because the runner now supports it natively (option a), or because the
  documented workaround (a compound `--cmd` or multiple `verify.js` invocations) is proven to
  work and is referenced from `bin/verify.js`'s own usage/help text or its skill documentation.
- If option (a): every one of the five hardcoded `'types'`/`'lint'` comparison sites is updated
  consistently — a partial update (e.g. widening the `allowed` set at line 212 but not the
  `suitesRun` filters at 387/451) would produce an inconsistent runner.
- `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Read all five call sites (`verify.js:212, 265, 281, 387, 451`) together before choosing an
approach — they must all agree on what counts as a "types-tier" check name, or the runner's
own internal bookkeeping (`suitesRun`, `staticNames`, the `allowed` set) will disagree with each
other. If choosing (a), define the widened match once (a shared predicate or regex, e.g.
`/^types(-|$)/`) and use it at every site rather than duplicating the pattern five times. If
choosing (b), the fix is documentation-only — add the guidance to `bin/verify.js`'s own
`--help`/usage text and to whichever skill file documents its `--cmd` naming convention for
callers.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` (lines 212, 265, 281, 387, 451) — the five call sites that would need a
  consistent widened match under option (a)
- Skill documentation for `/claude-tweaks:test` / `/claude-tweaks:build`'s verify.js invocation
  convention — where option (b)'s guidance would live, or where option (a)'s new naming
  convention would need documenting either way

## Gotchas

- This is a genuine design choice between (a) runner capability vs. (b) documented workaround —
  the record's own Deliverables frame both as valid; don't treat one as obviously correct without
  weighing the blast radius of changing shared verification-runner logic (option a) against the
  lower-risk, purely-documentary option (b).
- If choosing (a), verify the widened match doesn't accidentally capture an unrelated check name
  a caller might legitimately want in the post-tests tier (e.g. a check literally named
  `types-of-fun` that has nothing to do with typechecking) — a prefix match on `types-`/`types:`
  is a judgment call about false-positive risk, not a free lunch.

## Original request

**Summary:** bin/verify.js reserves only one "types" check name for the fail-fast-before-tests tier, but a monorepo can have multiple independent typecheck commands with no way to give more than one that treatment.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** bin/verify.js (the shared /claude-tweaks:test and /claude-tweaks:build verification runner)

**Use case:** A pnpm/npm workspace monorepo with multiple independently-typed packages (e.g. three packages each needing their own `tsc --noEmit`, with no single command that covers all three) wants typecheck and lint to run independently of whether `tests` happens to pass. verify.js's ordering policy treats exactly one `--cmd` name, `types`, as reserved for the "run before tests, fail-fast on failure" tier, alongside `lint`. Naming the extra typecheck commands something else (e.g. `types-core`, `types-worker`, `types-web`) demotes them to the "any other name" tier, which runs serially **after** `tests` succeeds under the same fail-fast policy — so when `tests` fails for a reason unrelated to any of the typechecks (e.g. a flaky test-hook timeout under concurrent machine load), all three typechecks get skipped (`skipped: fail-fast`) even though none of them actually depend on `tests` passing. A caller then has to notice the `skipped: fail-fast` rows and re-run each typecheck command by hand, outside the runner, to get a real signal.

**Suggested fix:** either (a) let multiple checks share the reserved pre-`tests` tier — e.g. any `--cmd` name prefixed `types:` or `types-` joins the same concurrent-with-lint, fail-fast-before-tests group the single `types` name gets today — or (b) document explicitly that a monorepo with N independent typecheck commands should invoke them as their own verify.js call (or combine them into one compound `--cmd types="a && b && c"`) rather than as N separately-named checks, so the fail-fast-skip behavior is expected rather than surprising.

**Reproduction:** `node bin/verify.js --cmd types-core="..." --cmd types-worker="..." --cmd types-web="..." --cmd lint="..." --cmd tests="..."` where `tests` fails for any reason — `report.json` shows `types-core`/`types-worker`/`types-web` as `{"skipped": "fail-fast"}` even though each is independent of `tests`.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.118.0

groups.title: verify/stamp.js: tmp filename shape changed silently; count-stamp write coverage lost
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review. Migrating `plugin/bin/lib/verify/stamp.js` off
the deleted `writeJsonAtomic` silently changed the temp filename shape from `${jsonPath}.tmp` to
`${basename}.tmp-${pid}` (confirmed, ~line 63: `writeFileAtomic(jsonPath, ...)`): the old
`lib/verify/atomic-write.js` used `const tmpPath = \`${filePath}.tmp\`;` while the replacement
(confirmed, `lib/atomic-write.js:27`) uses `path.join(dir, \`${path.basename(filePath)}.tmp-${process.pid}\`)`.
Any fixture, cleanup script, or `.gitignore` entry keyed on the old literal no longer matches.

Separately, `tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js:60`'s new pid-suffix pin covers only the
verify-pass stamp write; the count-stamp write migrated in the same commit (confirmed,
`verify.js:374`: `writeFileAtomic(countStampPath, ...)`) is unpinned. The deleted
`tests/bin-lib/verify/atomic-write.test.js` was the only place that had covered the count-stamp
write shape, and nothing replaced that coverage. The legacy bare-SHA twin write two lines below
the count-stamp call (confirmed, `stamp.js:69`: `const tmp = \`${legacyPath}.tmp\`;`) still uses

- Sweep for any remaining references to the old `.tmp` (no pid suffix) filename shape.
- Add a test pinning the count-stamp write's temp-filename shape, matching the coverage the

- Confirm the legacy bare-SHA twin write's un-migrated `.tmp` shape is intentional (it predates
  the pid-suffix convention) or migrate it too for consistency.

The count-stamp write path has an explicit test for its temp-file naming, and the legacy-write

   unrelated to this migration's collision-safety concern") to judge whether leaving it
   unmigrated was a deliberate scoping decision from the original PR, and either add a comment
   confirming that's still the right call, or migrate it to the same `writeFileAtomic` primitive
   for consistency if no reason to keep it separate survives scrutiny.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/stamp.js` (lines ~63, ~69) — the migrated JSON-stamp write and the

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` (line 374) — the count-stamp write, needs test coverage
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` (~line 60) — add the count-stamp temp-filename test

## Gotchas

- The legacy twin write's own code comment already states it was deliberately left untouched
  ("Non-Goals") — don't assume this is an oversight without reading that reasoning first; the
  fix may be "confirm and document," not "migrate."
- Scope the `.tmp`-reference sweep to this migration's own affected files — a repo-wide grep for
  bare `.tmp` will surface many unrelated hits (other modules' own temp-file conventions) that
  are out of scope for this record.

## Original request

## Current State
Found during a pre-release whole-branch review. Migrating `plugin/bin/lib/verify/stamp.js` off the deleted `writeJsonAtomic` silently changed the temp filename shape from `${jsonPath}.tmp` to `${basename}.tmp-${pid}` (~line 63): the old `lib/verify/atomic-write.js` used `const tmpPath = \`${filePath}.tmp\`;` while the replacement (`lib/atomic-write.js:27`) uses `path.join(dir, \`${path.basename(filePath)}.tmp-${process.pid}\`)`. The deleted tests/bin-lib/verify/atomic-write.test.js was the only place that had covered the count-stamp write shape, and nothing replaced that coverage. The legacy bare-SHA twin write two lines below the count-stamp call still uses the old `${legacyPath}.tmp` shape, unmigrated.

groups.title: verify.js/#2026: the only new test doesn't exercise the real behavior change (empty flaky allowlist)
groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `tests/`. #2026's change to
`plugin/bin/verify.js` (confirmed, ~line 305: `const retryHook = async (result, ctx) => { if
(!decl) return result; ...`) replaced `flakyEnabled = Boolean(decl && decl.flaky.files.length >
0)` with `if (!decl) return result`, per that change's own comment: "an empty/absent `flaky`
declaration still needs a `retryDecision.reason` recorded." `declaration.js`'s `readDeclaration`
(confirmed, ~line 126: `let flaky = { files: [], maxRetries: DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES };`) always
defaults `flaky = { files: [], ... }`, so the empty-allowlist case is the *only* new behavior
this change introduces.

`tests/bin-lib/verify/cli.test.js:1103` (`noParseArgs`, the only new test in this range,
confirmed present) declares `flaky: { files: ['tests/flaky.test.js'] }` — a non-empty allowlist.
No test in the file exercises an empty or absent `flaky` declaration, so the actual behavior
change this record shipped is untested — it passes identically before and after the fix.

## Deliverables

Add a test that supplies an empty or absent `flaky` declaration and asserts
`retryDecision.reason` is recorded as the change's comment describes.

## Acceptance Criteria

The new test fails against a revert of #2026's `verify.js` change (proving it actually exercises
the behavior) and passes on the current code.

## Technical Approach

Add a new test case alongside the existing `noParseArgs`-based test at
`tests/bin-lib/verify/cli.test.js:1103`, using a declaration with either no `flaky` key at all,
or `flaky: { files: [] }` explicitly — following the same test fixture shape (`tmpGitRepo`,
`noParseArgs` or an equivalent args builder) the existing test already uses. Assert
`retryDecision.reason` is present in the check's recorded result even though `decl.flaky.files`
is empty, and verify-before-committing per this record's own Acceptance Criteria: temporarily
revert the `if (!decl) return result` line back to the pre-#2026
`Boolean(decl && decl.flaky.files.length > 0)` shape locally and confirm the new test actually
fails, proving it exercises the real behavior change rather than something that would pass
either way.

### Key Files

  code doesn't actually cover the behavior change #2026 shipped.
- Use the exact declaration shape `declaration.js`'s default produces (`{ files: [], maxRetries:
